title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
皇上御極之十一年爲弘治戊午
天下例當鄉試河南
臣白于巡按監察御史李〔瀚〕
走幣聘〔琰〕及教授李濬學正
李〔元宏〕教諭周〔昂〕〔汝南〕毛
〔鵬〕孟〔震〕林〔韜〕訓導林〔世瑞〕郭
===
〔名世〕以司文衡先是巡撫右
副都御史陳〔道〕偕〔瀚〕以貢院
爲禮羅賢才要地卑隘弗治
殆非所宜乃協謀鎮守太監
監〔忠〕清戎監察御史〔□章〕檄
所司充拓改作其布〔□〕結構
悉費心思而整飭壯麗甲
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

皇上御極之十一年，爲弘治戊午，天下例當鄉試。河南臣白于巡按監察御史李〔瀚〕，走幣聘〔琰〕及教授李濬、學正李〔元宏〕、教諭周〔昂〕〔汝南〕、毛〔鵬〕、孟〔震〕、林〔韜〕、訓導林〔世瑞〕、郭〔名世〕，以司文衡。先是，巡撫右副都御史陳〔道〕偕〔瀚〕，以貢院爲禮羅賢才要地，卑隘弗治，殆非所宜，乃協謀鎮守太監監〔忠〕、清戎監察御史〔□章〕，檄所司充拓改作。其布〔□〕結構，悉費心思，而整飭壯麗甲
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

The eleventh year since His Majesty ascended the throne was the wuwu year of the Hongzhi reign [1498], when, according to established practice, Provincial Examinations were due throughout the realm. In Henan, your servant reported to the Regional Inspecting Censor Li Han [?]. Gifts were promptly dispatched to invite Yan, together with Prefectural School Professor Li Jun, Departmental School Instructor Li Yuanhong, County School Instructors Zhou Ang (Runan [?]), Mao Peng, Meng Zhen, and Lin Tao, and Assistant Instructors Lin Shirui and Guo Mingshi, to oversee the assessment of literary merit.

Previously, the Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Dao, together with Li Han, had considered that the examination compound was an important place for courteously recruiting worthy talent, and that its low, cramped, and neglected condition was wholly inappropriate. They therefore consulted jointly with the Regional Commandant, Grand Eunuch Jian Zhong [?], and the Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military affairs, □ Zhang [?], and issued orders to the responsible offices to enlarge and rebuild it. Its layout [?] and construction received painstaking attention, and in orderliness, grandeur, and beauty it ranked foremost …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
多省既而崙復以職專監臨
合提學副使卑璽所取七郡
士嚴加覆試而又增一户遺
總一千八百人有奇八月庚
午入院觀蒞偉觀百司皆慶
幸從事而試士之操觚染翰
者亦廣其心目文思川涌自
覺倍於常日庚寅撤棘遵
===
制額取八十人第其氏名錄其
文之尤者將獻于
上錄成故事𤦺當序諸首竊惟我
朝自
聖祖開科以來迄今百三十餘年
兩京及十三省鄉試作序者
punctuated:
多省。既而崙復以職專監臨，合提學副使卑璽所取七郡士，嚴加覆試，而又增一户遺，總一千八百人有奇。八月庚午入院，觀蒞偉觀，百司皆慶幸從事，而試士之操觚染翰者亦廣其心目，文思川涌，自覺倍於常日。庚寅撤棘，遵制額取八十人，第其氏名，錄其文之尤者，將獻于上。
錄成，故事，𤦺當序諸首。竊惟我朝自聖祖開科以來，迄今百三十餘年，兩京及十三省鄉試作序者
translation_en:
…many provinces. Thereafter Lun, whose official duties included sole responsibility for supervision, assembled the candidates from the seven prefectures selected by Bei Xi [?], the Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and subjected them to a rigorous reexamination. Further additions were made from among those omitted [?], bringing the total to somewhat more than eighteen hundred. On the gengwu day of the eighth month, they entered the examination compound and beheld its imposing appearance [?]. All the officials considered themselves fortunate to take part. The candidates taking up their writing tablets and wetting their brushes likewise found their minds and vision broadened. Their literary inspiration surged like a river, and they felt it to be twice that of ordinary days. On the gengyin day, the thorn barriers were removed. In accordance with the imperially prescribed quota, eighty men were selected. Their names were listed in ranked order, and the finest of their compositions were transcribed for presentation to His Majesty.
When the record was completed, precedent required that I, Qi, write a preface for its beginning. I humbly reflect that more than a hundred and thirty years have now passed since our dynasty’s Sagely Progenitor inaugurated the examinations. Those who have written prefaces for Provincial Examination records in the two capitals and the thirteen provinces…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
多矣其戒勉諸士子者諄且
盡矣唉不佞不敢爲贊詞〔祇〕
請以目所擊者相告　予監
臨方作新貢院之餘百方綜
理至如一門之設亦必加手
書於其上拳拳以公私理欲
天地鬼神鑒照之言相警畏比鎖
===
院額
天矣詞有曰凡狥私利顛倒是非
神降百殃奪官殄祀聞者毛
髮爲之森竪其敬事慎選之
心無非欲爲
朝廷得真才以輔成
聖天子億萬年之盛治也即其小
punctuated: 多矣，其戒勉諸士子者諄且盡矣。唉！不佞不敢爲贊詞，〔祇〕請以目所擊者相告。予監臨方作新貢院之餘，百方綜理，至如一門之設，亦必加手書於其上，拳拳以公私理欲、天地鬼神鑒照之言相警畏。比鎖院，額天矣。詞有曰：「凡狥私利，顛倒是非，神降百殃，奪官殄祀。」聞者毛髮爲之森竪。其敬事慎選之心，無非欲爲朝廷得真才，以輔成聖天子億萬年之盛治也。即其小
translation_en: …have been many, and their admonitions and encouragement to the candidates have been earnest and exhaustive. Ah! I, unworthy as I am, dare not compose words of praise; 〔I merely〕 ask leave to relate what I have witnessed. Our Supervising Official, having just renovated the examination compound, attended to its management in every way. Even when a single gate was installed, he would place his own handwritten inscription above it. With earnest words concerning public duty and private interest, moral principle and selfish desire, and the scrutiny of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, he urged mutual vigilance and reverence. When the compound was sealed, he addressed Heaven [?]. His words included: “Whoever pursues private gain and confounds right and wrong shall suffer a hundred calamities sent down by the spirits, be stripped of office, and have his ancestral sacrifices extinguished.” Those who heard this felt their hair stand on end. His dedication to his duties and care in selecting candidates sprang entirely from his desire to obtain men of true ability for the court, to help bring about the flourishing rule of the sagely Son of Heaven for countless ages. From these small matters…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
而可以卜其大諸士子行將
再試春官奉
廷對以有官守宜何如才爲念
哉亦惟曰
國家之所以教育我也何厚有
司之所以簡拔我也何重以
其所學充其所用隨其職之
所在立言立政一以公不狃
===
以私絀以理不狥以欲對越
天地而無愧質鬼神而無疑必
如監臨之戒誓以成光明俊
偉之業使人皆曰某科得人
之盛某主司之所取也次等
將求能踵前輩稱公且明者
punctuated: 而可以卜其大。諸士子行將再試春官，奉廷對，以有官守，宜何如才爲念哉？亦惟曰：「國家之所以教育我也何厚！有司之所以簡拔我也何重！」以其所學充其所用，隨其職之所在，立言立政，一以公，不狃以私，絀以理，不狥以欲，對越天地而無愧，質鬼神而無疑。必如監臨之戒誓，以成光明俊偉之業，使人皆曰：「某科得人之盛，某主司之所取也。」次等將求能踵前輩稱公且明者
translation_en: …and from this one can judge the greater matters. You candidates will soon sit again for the examination administered by the Ministry of Rites, present your answers at the Palace Examination, and assume official responsibilities. What, then, should you take to heart [?]? Simply reflect: “How generously the state has educated us! How weighty is the responsibility with which the authorities have selected us!” Put what you have learned fully into practice. Wherever your duties lie, let your pronouncements and measures be governed entirely by impartiality. Do not become habituated to private interests; submit to principle and do not yield to desire. Stand before Heaven and Earth without shame, and submit yourselves to the scrutiny of spirits without misgiving. You must abide by the Supervising Official’s admonitions and oath, thereby accomplishing illustrious and outstanding deeds, so that everyone will say: “What an abundance of worthy men that examination obtained! They were selected by such-and-such an Examiner.” Those of the next rank [?] will seek to follow predecessors acclaimed as impartial and discerning…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
芳躅亦將藉有明鑑之稱而
無濫竽之誚矣諸士子倘無
忽迂謬爲留經人道而取
佩弦韋則本必無小補云維
時內而提調則左布政使王
〔珣〕右布政使徐〔鏞〕監試則按
察使鄧〔庠〕副使張〔鼐〕與監臨
===
實同心德外而防範則左參
政張〔璥〕右參政顧〔福〕祝〔徑〕副
使李〔經〕劉〔俊〕左參議粟〔紹宗〕
羅〔鑒〕僉事包〔裕〕彭〔綱〕馬〔騆〕閻
〔璽〕皆竭力殫心而百執事亦
未嘗有一之敢怠荒者焉猗
歟盛哉
punctuated:
芳躅，亦將藉有明鑑之稱，而無濫竽之誚矣。諸士子倘無忽迂謬，爲留經人道而取佩弦韋，則本必無小補云。
維時，內而提調則左布政使王〔珣〕、右布政使徐〔鏞〕，監試則按察使鄧〔庠〕、副使張〔鼐〕，與監臨實同心德。外而防範則左參政張〔璥〕、右參政顧〔福〕、祝〔徑〕、副使李〔經〕、劉〔俊〕、左參議粟〔紹宗〕、羅〔鑒〕、僉事包〔裕〕、彭〔綱〕、馬〔騆〕、閻〔璽〕，皆竭力殫心，而百執事亦未嘗有一之敢怠荒者焉。猗歟，盛哉！
translation_en:
…illustrious footsteps, and thereby also gain a reputation for discerning judgment, without being reproached as an incompetent filling a position. If the candidates do not disregard these rambling and mistaken words, but attend to the human way [?] and adopt them as corrective reminders—like wearing a bowstring or a leather thong—then they will surely be of no small benefit [?].
At this time, those serving within as Proctors were Wang Xun, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Xu Yong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Deng Xiang, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Zhang Nai, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. They were truly united in purpose and principle with the Supervising Official.
Those responsible for external security were Zhang Jing, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Gu Fu and Zhu Jing, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners; Li Jing and Liu Jun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Su Shaozong and Luo Jian, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners; and Bao Yu, Peng Gang, Ma Diao, and Yan Xi, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. All devoted their utmost strength and attention to their duties. Nor was there a single person among all the functionaries who dared to be negligent or remiss. Ah, how splendid!

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
山東萊州府儒學教授濮〔琰〕
謹序
punctuated: 山東萊州府儒學教授濮〔琰〕謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Pu Yan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong.

text:

河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使王□〔德潤山東曹縣人　乙丑進士〕

punctuated:
弘治十一年鄉試

監臨官
巡按河南監察御史李瀚〔叔淵，山西沁水縣人，辛丑進士〕。

提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使王□〔德潤，山東曹縣人，乙丑進士〕。
河南等處承宣布政使司右布政使徐鏞〔用和，直隸興國州人，己□□士〕。

河南等處提刑按察司按察使鄧庠〔宗周，湖廣宜章縣人，壬辰進士〕。

直隸保定府安州儒學學正李充宏〔擴之，浙江黃巖縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
江西南昌府寧縣儒學教諭周昂〔廷舉，直隸祁門縣人，丙午貢士〕。
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭王汝南〔汝金，浙江慈谿縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

translation_en:
Provincial Examination of the Eleventh Year of Hongzhi (1498)

Supervising Official
Li Han, Regional Investigating Censor for Henan, had the courtesy name Shuyuan and was a native of Qinshui County, Shanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the xinchou year.

Proctors
Wang □, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan, had the courtesy name Derun and was a native of Cao County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Xu Yong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan, had the courtesy name Yonghe and was a native of Xingguo Subprefecture, Zhili [?]. His qualification is recorded as “ji□□shi” [?].

Examination Monitoring Officials
Deng Xiang, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Henan, had the courtesy name Zongzhou and was a native of Yizhang County, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.
Zhang Nai, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Henan, had the courtesy name Yonghe and was a native of Licheng County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.

Examiners
Pu Yan, Prefectural School Professor of Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Tingfang and was a native of Dangtu County, Zhili. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the guimao year.
Li Jun, Prefectural School Professor of Yingtian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shizhe and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners
Li Chonghong, Subprefectural School Director of Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Kuozhi and was a native of Huangyan County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the guimao year.
Zhou Ang, County School Instructor of Ning County [?], Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Tingju and was a native of Qimen County, Zhili. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.
Wang Runan, County School Instructor of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Rujin and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the yimao year.
Mao Peng, County School Instructor of Fanchang County, Taiping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Wenju and was a native of □□ County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the guimao year.
An official whose name ends in Zhen, with his title and the preceding portion of his name illegible (□□□□震) [?], served at the Confucian school of Liuyang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Shiming, and he was a native of Guizhou Guard, Guizhou. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
廣西柳州府賓州上林縣儒學教諭孫鼐〔時用廣東東莞縣人　己酉貢士〕
浙江紹興府嵊縣儒學訓導林世瑞〔廷覲福建閩縣人　癸卯貢士〕
順天府通州儒學訓導鄭岳〔晦夫山西安邑縣人　乙卯貢士〕
印卷官
河南等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷曹琚〔廷用陝西郃陽縣人　癸卯貢士〕
河南等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷謝慶〔以興湖廣黃岡縣人　丁酉貢士〕

===
受卷官
河南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨翟敬〔行簡山西猗氏縣人　庚戌進士〕

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子於鄉黨恂恂如也似不能言者其在
宗廟朝廷便便言唯謹爾
君子之中庸也君子而時中
以君命將之再拜稽首而受其後廩人繼
粟庖人繼肉不以君命將之
易
庸言之信庸行之謹閑邪存其誠
===
健而說決而和
言行君子之所以動天地也可不慎乎
是故履德之基也謙德之柄也復德之本
也恒德之固也損德之脩也益德之
裕也困德之辨也井德之地也巽德
之制也
書
九敘惟歌戒之用休董之用威勸之以九
歌
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

孔子於鄉黨，恂恂如也，似不能言者；其在宗廟朝廷，便便言，唯謹爾。

君子之中庸也，君子而時中。

以君命將之，再拜稽首而受。其後廩人繼粟，庖人繼肉，不以君命將之。

易

庸言之信，庸行之謹，閑邪存其誠。

健而說，決而和。

言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎？

是故履，德之基也；謙，德之柄也；復，德之本也；恒，德之固也；損，德之脩也；益，德之裕也；困，德之辨也；井，德之地也；巽，德之制也。

書

九敘惟歌，戒之用休，董之用威，勸之以九歌。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

In his native community, Confucius was respectful and unassuming, as though unable to speak. In the ancestral temple and at court, he spoke fluently, yet always with care.

The gentleman exemplifies the Mean because he is a gentleman and accords with the Mean as circumstances require.

When the gift was presented in the ruler’s name, he bowed twice, touched his forehead to the ground, and accepted it. Thereafter, the granary keeper continued to supply grain and the cook continued to supply meat, without presenting them in the ruler’s name.

Book of Changes

Be trustworthy in ordinary speech and careful in ordinary conduct; guard against evil and preserve sincerity.

Vigorous yet joyous; resolute yet harmonious.

Words and deeds are the means by which the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be careful?

Thus, Treading (Lü) is the foundation of virtue; Modesty (Qian) is its handle; Return (Fu) is its root; Constancy (Heng) is its firmness; Decrease (Sun) is its cultivation; Increase (Yi) is its abundance; Adversity (Kun) is its discernment; the Well (Jing) is its ground; and the Gentle (Xun) is its regulation.

Book of Documents

Let the nine achievements, duly ordered, be celebrated in song. Admonish them with auspicious words, supervise them with authority, and encourage them with the nine songs.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
伊洛瀍澗既入于河滎波既豬導□□□
孟豬厥土惟壤下土墳壚厥田惟中□
上厥賦錯上中厥貢漆枲絺紵厥篚
纖纊錫貢磬錯
斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
穆穆在上明明在下灼于四方罔不惟德
之勤
詩
我覯之子袞衣繡裳
===
鐘鼓既設舉醻逸逸
王猶允塞徐方既來徐方既同天子之功
四方既平徐方來庭徐方不回王曰
還歸
烈文辟公錫茲祉福惠我無疆子孫保之
無封靡于爾邦維王其崇之念茲戎
功繼序其皇之無競維人四方其訓
之不顯維德百辟其刑之於乎前王
不忘
punctuated:
伊洛瀍澗既入于河，滎波既豬，導□□□孟豬。厥土惟壤，下土墳壚。厥田惟中□上，厥賦錯上中。厥貢漆枲絺紵，厥篚纖纊，錫貢磬錯。

斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。

穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。

詩

我覯之子，袞衣繡裳。

鐘鼓既設，舉醻逸逸。

王猶允塞，徐方既來。徐方既同，天子之功。四方既平，徐方來庭。徐方不回，王曰：「還歸。」

烈文辟公，錫茲祉福。惠我無疆，子孫保之。無封靡于爾邦，維王其崇之。念茲戎功，繼序其皇之。無競維人，四方其訓之。不顯維德，百辟其刑之。於乎！前王不忘。
translation_en:
The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers had entered the Yellow River; the waters of Yingbo had been gathered into a reservoir. Waters were channeled [three illegible characters] Mengzhu [?]. The soil was loam; in the lowlands it was rich, dark earth. The fields were graded middle [illegible character] upper [?], and the tax assessment varied within the upper-middle grade. The tribute consisted of lacquer, hemp, fine kudzu cloth, and ramie cloth; the tribute baskets contained fine silk and silk floss. By command, sounding stones and stones for polishing were also presented as tribute.

Gather these five blessings, and bestow them widely upon the common people.

Reverent and dignified are those above; clear-sighted are those below. Their brilliance shines throughout the four quarters, and none fails to apply himself diligently to virtue.

The Book of Odes

I behold that noble man, wearing a dragon-patterned robe and an embroidered lower garment.

The bells and drums have been set out; they offer toasts in easy harmony.

The king’s plans were truly fulfilled: the people of Xu came in submission. That Xu was brought into accord was the achievement of the Son of Heaven. The four quarters had been pacified, and Xu came to court. Xu did not turn away from allegiance. The king said, “Return home.”

Illustrious and cultured lords, you bestow these blessings and good fortune. Your beneficence toward us has no bounds; may our descendants preserve it. Be neither excessive nor wasteful in your states, and the king will honor you. Remember these great achievements; may your successors magnify them. Nothing is stronger than worthy men: the four quarters will follow their instruction. Is not virtue illustrious? The many lords will take it as their model. Ah! The former kings are not forgotten.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋八月庚辰公及戎盟于唐〔隱公二年春〕
王正月公如齊　夏仲孫蔑如京師〔俱宣公九年〕
初獻六羽〔隱公五年〕　初稅畝〔宣公十五年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人同盟于清丘〔宣公十二年〕
秋七月辛巳豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十七年〕　叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公
===
子圍齊國弱宋向戌衛齊惡陳公子
招蔡公孫歸生鄭罕虎許人曹人于
虢〔昭公元年〕　夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯
許男徐子滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾
子宋世子佐淮夷會于申　遂滅賴
〔俱昭公四年〕　叔弓如晉〔昭公八年〕　秋
公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕
punctuated:
春秋

秋八月庚辰，公及戎盟于唐。〔隱公二年春〕
王正月，公如齊。夏，仲孫蔑如京師。〔俱宣公九年〕
初獻六羽。〔隱公五年〕初稅畝。〔宣公十五年〕
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘。〔宣公十二年〕
秋七月辛巳，豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋。〔襄公二十七年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。〔昭公元年〕夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申，遂滅賴。〔俱昭公四年〕叔弓如晉。〔昭公八年〕秋，公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘。〔昭公十三年〕
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the eighth month, on the gengchen day, the duke made a covenant with the Rong at Tang. 〔Spring of the second year of Duke Yin [?]; the annotation conflicts with “autumn” in the text.〕

In the first month of the royal calendar, the duke went to Qi. In summer, Zhongsun Mie went to the royal capital. 〔Both in the ninth year of Duke Xuan.〕

For the first time, the feather dance was performed in six rows. 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin.〕 For the first time, fields were taxed by the mu. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕

Representatives of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao entered into a common covenant at Qingqiu. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕

In autumn, in the seventh month, on the xinsi day, Bao made a covenant with the grandees of the regional lords at Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕

Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕

In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu 許, the Viscount of Xu 徐, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen 沈, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi assembled at Shen 申. They then destroyed Lai. 〔Both in the fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Shu Gong went to Jin. 〔Eighth year of Duke Zhao.〕

In autumn, the duke met at Pingqiu with the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
禮記
未賜圭瓚則資鬯於天子天子命之教□
後為學
是故禮者君之大柄也所以別嫌明微儐
鬼神考制度別仁義所以治政安君
也
故聽其雅頌之聲志意得廣焉
事君大言入則望大利
第貳場
===
論
脩德致和以契天地之心
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢命二千石撫循百姓詔〔建武六年〕
擬唐以姚元之為兵部尚書同中書門下
三品誥〔開元元年〕
擬宋以程頤為崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元
年〕
判語五條
punctuated:
禮記

未賜圭瓚，則資鬯於天子。天子命之教，□後為學。

是故禮者，君之大柄也，所以別嫌明微，儐鬼神，考制度，別仁義，所以治政安君也。

故聽其雅頌之聲，志意得廣焉。

事君，大言入，則望大利。

第貳場

論

脩德致和，以契天地之心。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕

擬漢命二千石撫循百姓詔〔建武六年〕。

擬唐以姚元之為兵部尚書同中書門下三品誥〔開元元年〕。

擬宋以程頤為崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元年〕。

判語五條。
translation_en:
Record of Rites

If one has not been granted a jade libation ladle, one obtains the sacrificial aromatic wine from the Son of Heaven. The Son of Heaven commands him to teach; only [?] afterward does he establish a school.

Thus ritual is the ruler’s great instrument: through it he distinguishes doubtful matters, makes subtle distinctions clear, honors ghosts and spirits, examines institutions and regulations, and distinguishes benevolence and righteousness. Through it he orders government and secures the ruler.

Thus, on hearing the sounds of the Elegantiae and Hymns, one’s aspirations and thoughts are broadened.

In serving a ruler, when one’s counsel on great matters is accepted, one looks for great benefit.

Second Session

Discourse

Cultivate virtue and bring about harmony, thereby according with the heart of Heaven and Earth.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question in this category [?].〕

Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor commanding officials of two-thousand-bushel rank to nurture and care for the common people. 〔Sixth year of Jianwu.〕

Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Yao Yuanzhi Minister of War and Grand Councilor with third-rank status in the Secretariat–Chancellery. 〔First year of Kaiyuan.〕

Compose a memorial of thanks in the voice of Cheng Yi of the Song upon his appointment as Lecturer in Chongzheng Hall. 〔First year of Yuanyou.〕

Five legal judgments.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
擧用有過官吏
甲紉私擅用財
禁止師巫邪術
縱放軍人歇役
詐欺官私取財
第叁場
第五道
問我
國家
===
聖聖相承萬幾之暇皆有著述以昭示天下萬
世臣民浩瀚該博未易悉舉伏覩
英宗睿皇帝憲綱一書專爲憲臣而作盖述
列聖之意以成言有憲綱有憲體有禮儀有事
例有條格隆之以採訪彈奏之任專之
以督察平反之柄而其訓戒之詞不曰
存心則曰持身不曰循理則曰守法是
又進之以向上之功本之以檢身之學
其所以爲憲臣謀者至矣夫考古證今
punctuated:
擧用有過官吏。
甲紉私擅用財。
禁止師巫邪術。
縱放軍人歇役。
詐欺官私取財。

第叁場
第五道

問：我國家聖聖相承，萬幾之暇，皆有著述，以昭示天下萬世臣民，浩瀚該博，未易悉舉。伏覩英宗睿皇帝《憲綱》一書，專爲憲臣而作，盖述列聖之意以成言。有憲綱，有憲體，有禮儀，有事例，有條格。隆之以採訪彈奏之任，專之以督察平反之柄。而其訓戒之詞，不曰存心，則曰持身；不曰循理，則曰守法。是又進之以向上之功，本之以檢身之學。其所以爲憲臣謀者至矣。夫考古證今，
translation_en:
Recommending and employing officials and clerks with past offenses.
Unauthorized private use of funds [?].
Prohibiting the illicit arts of spirit mediums and shamans.
Allowing military personnel to leave and cease performing their duties.
Obtaining government or private property by fraud.

Third Session
Fifth Question

Question: In our dynasty, sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign. In the intervals between their myriad duties, all have composed writings to instruct clearly the subjects of the realm for all generations. These writings are so vast and comprehensive that they cannot readily be enumerated in full. I have reverently perused Emperor Yingzong Rui’s book, the Outline of Censorial Regulations (Xiangang), composed expressly for censorial officials. It gives written expression to the intentions of the successive sage sovereigns. It contains guiding principles for censorial work, standards of censorial conduct, ceremonial prescriptions, precedents, and regulations. It dignifies these officials with responsibility for gathering information and submitting impeachments, and entrusts them with authority to supervise, investigate, and redress wrongful judgments. Its admonitions speak either of maintaining a proper heart or of conducting oneself properly, either of following principle or of observing the law. Thus it further encourages their efforts toward moral improvement and grounds their work in the discipline of examining their own conduct. Its provision for censorial officials is indeed consummate. Now, examining antiquity to substantiate the present…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
儒者事也請據風憲一事為諸生言之
書曰爾陳時臬亭周官小宰掌建邦之
宮刑此風憲之始也秦漢以後御史典
糾察之任而所居之署更改不時所任
之官崇卑不一當時有執法蘭臺百僚
敬服者有執法殿中公卿畏憚者有持
平無私時君稱之者有恩不假人宰相
畏之者漢時遣繡衣直指行郡國而不
常置唐以後始有按察觀察採訪處置
===
提刑等銜而所遣之人多寡不一所限
之期久近不同當時有衣繡持斧出捕
盜賊者有繩糾吏治所至震慴者有覆
訊冤獄全活甚多者有作詩諭民強暴
知悔者古今之所歆羨載籍之所襃美
不能一一詳說其間亦有存心持身之
無愧而內可格非外可及物者乎我
國家尤重風憲內設都察院十三道外設按
察司分司內外相維長貳相承于
punctuated:
儒者事也，請據風憲一事為諸生言之。《書》曰：「爾陳時臬亭。」《周官》小宰掌建邦之宮刑，此風憲之始也。秦漢以後，御史典糾察之任，而所居之署更改不時，所任之官崇卑不一。當時有執法蘭臺，百僚敬服者；有執法殿中，公卿畏憚者；有持平無私，時君稱之者；有恩不假人，宰相畏之者。漢時遣繡衣直指行郡國，而不常置。唐以後始有按察、觀察、採訪、處置、提刑等銜，而所遣之人多寡不一，所限之期久近不同。當時有衣繡持斧，出捕盜賊者；有繩糾吏治，所至震慴者；有覆訊冤獄，全活甚多者；有作詩諭民，強暴知悔者。古今之所歆羨，載籍之所襃美，不能一一詳說。其間亦有存心持身之無愧，而內可格非、外可及物者乎？

我國家尤重風憲，內設都察院十三道，外設按察司分司，內外相維，長貳相承，于
translation_en:
…is the business of Confucian scholars. Allow me to address you students on the particular subject of censorial oversight. The Book of Documents says: “You are to set forth these standards [亭?].” In the Offices of Zhou, the Junior Steward was responsible for establishing the penal rules governing the royal palace. These were the beginnings of censorial oversight. From the Qin and Han onward, censors held responsibility for investigating and impeaching misconduct, but the offices in which they served changed at irregular intervals, and their official ranks varied in standing. Among them were men who enforced the law at the Orchid Terrace and won the respect and submission of all officials; men who enforced the law within the palace halls and inspired dread among dukes and ministers; men whose impartiality and selflessness earned their sovereign’s praise; and men who did not delegate the dispensing of favors [?] and whom chief ministers feared.

Under the Han, Direct-Reporting Emissaries in Embroidered Garments were dispatched to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, but these were not permanent appointments. From the Tang onward, titles such as Surveillance Commissioner, Surveillance Commissioner of a Circuit, Investigation Commissioner, Disposition Commissioner, and Judicial Commissioner began to appear. The number of men dispatched varied, as did the length of their prescribed terms. Among them were men who went out in embroidered garments, bearing axes of authority, to apprehend bandits; men who investigated and corrected official administration, inspiring fear wherever they went; men who reexamined unjust criminal cases and saved many lives; and men who composed poems to admonish the people, bringing even the violent and overbearing to repentance. Those admired throughout the ages and praised in written records are too numerous to discuss individually in detail. Among them, were there also men whose intentions and personal conduct were beyond reproach, who could inwardly correct their sovereign’s errors and outwardly extend benefits to others?

Our dynasty places particular importance on censorial oversight. At the capital it has established the Censorate with its thirteen circuits, and in the provinces, Provincial Surveillance Commissions and their branch offices. The central and provincial authorities sustain one another, while their principal and subordinate officials carry on their duties in succession. This has continued for …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
今百數十年永遵守不改□□□□□
有常額非若前代之更易無定制
睿皇之書誨之諄諄是宜共成貞爾之政以濟
昇平之治嘗觀今日持憲之臣類皆老
成諳練之士講讀
聖訓蓋有素矣然皂囊之疏相繼於
彤庭而或遺當務之急星度之輅交馳於郡
縣而尚多未雪之冤豈知之而不言不
行歟抑有所未知歟或於
===
聖訓所謂明白正大忠厚詳慎者體之未至持
之不誠歟抑勢有所拘力有所不逮歟
夫居其位而不知不智也知之而不言
不行不忠也勢拘之力限之而不能去
不勇也諸生行當有官守言責孔子曰
如或知爾則何以哉
問古者諫不設官而天下皆可諫之人廷
無時諱而臣庶皆可言之士此德澤所
以周流扞衛所以屏伏也後世諫有□
punctuated:
今百數十年，永遵守不改。□□□□□有常額，非若前代之更易無定制。睿皇之書，誨之諄諄，是宜共成貞爾之政，以濟昇平之治。嘗觀今日持憲之臣，類皆老成諳練之士，講讀聖訓，蓋有素矣。然皂囊之疏相繼於彤庭，而或遺當務之急；星度之輅交馳於郡縣，而尚多未雪之冤。豈知之而不言不行歟？抑有所未知歟？或於聖訓所謂明白正大、忠厚詳慎者，體之未至，持之不誠歟？抑勢有所拘，力有所不逮歟？夫居其位而不知，不智也；知之而不言不行，不忠也；勢拘之、力限之而不能去，不勇也。諸生行當有官守言責。孔子曰：「如或知爾，則何以哉？」

問：古者諫不設官，而天下皆可諫之人；廷無時諱，而臣庶皆可言之士。此德澤所以周流，扞衛所以屏伏也。後世諫有□
translation_en:
…now for more than a hundred years, these arrangements have continually been observed without alteration. [Five illegible characters] have fixed quotas, unlike the frequent changes and lack of settled institutions under previous dynasties. The august emperor’s writings offer earnest instruction. Those concerned should therefore work together to achieve upright administration [?] and contribute to peaceful government. I have observed that today’s officials charged with disciplinary oversight are generally mature and experienced men, long accustomed to expounding and studying the imperial instructions. Yet although memorials enclosed in black pouches arrive in succession at the vermilion court, urgent matters are sometimes overlooked; although the carriages of inspecting officials [?] travel back and forth through prefectures and counties, many injustices remain unredressed. Do they know of these matters but fail to speak or act? Or are there things they do not know? Or have they failed fully to embody, or sincerely to uphold, what the imperial instructions call clarity, uprightness, loyalty, generosity, thoroughness, and caution? Or are they constrained by circumstances, with powers insufficient to accomplish their tasks?

To hold office without knowing its business is to lack wisdom. To know but neither speak nor act is to lack loyalty. To be constrained by circumstances and limited in one’s powers, yet be unable to leave office, is to lack courage. You students will soon have official duties and responsibilities to speak out. Confucius said: “If someone were to recognize your abilities, what would you do?”

Question: In antiquity, no special offices were established for remonstrance, and everyone in the realm could remonstrate. At court there were no taboos imposed by the times, and officials and commoners alike could speak. This was how the ruler’s beneficence circulated everywhere and how protective forces remained out of sight [?]. In later ages, remonstrance had [illegible]…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
員諫大夫設於何人諫議大夫改於何
代置拾遺補闕置司諫正言又見於何
君其間有諫封上林之令毅上林之麗
者有諫幸甘泉之獵願誅佞臣者或謂
受諫不及貞觀而又諫同州之校獵或
謂瓜果不必授官而又止拜相之白麻
以武臣立功當遷而堅執以為請以君
命取信於下而抗言不可更賢者不能
留也欲留之者以其有山陵之功不肯
===
者不能去也欲去之者不待其山陵之
畢此皆善諫而盡職者可一一言之歟
又聞諫之道有直有諷犯顏逆鱗不顧
剖心之誅古之直也後世以直自許者
或陰黨邪謀阿附奸慝古之直殆不如
此也微言婉辭託意於詩書之旨古之
諷也後世以諷自名者或啓想神僊恣
心遊樂古之諷殆不如是也昔人謂下
之不諫其弊不三弊果可去乎諫之法
punctuated: 員。諫大夫設於何人？諫議大夫改於何代？置拾遺、補闕，置司諫、正言，又見於何君？其間有諫封上林之令、毅上林之麗者，有諫幸甘泉之獵、願誅佞臣者；或謂受諫不及貞觀，而又諫同州之校獵；或謂瓜果不必授官，而又止拜相之白麻；以武臣立功當遷，而堅執以為請；以君命取信於下，而抗言不可更。賢者不能留也，欲留之者以其有山陵之功；不肯者不能去也，欲去之者不待其山陵之畢。此皆善諫而盡職者，可一一言之歟？又聞諫之道有直有諷。犯顏逆鱗，不顧剖心之誅，古之直也。後世以直自許者，或陰黨邪謀，阿附奸慝，古之直殆不如此也。微言婉辭，託意於詩書之旨，古之諷也。後世以諷自名者，或啓想神僊，恣心遊樂，古之諷殆不如是也。昔人謂下之不諫，其弊不三，弊果可去乎？諫之法
translation_en:
…officials. Under whom was the office of Grand Master of Remonstrance established? In which dynasty was it renamed Grand Master of Remonstrance and Counsel? Under which rulers were the offices of Reminder and Rectifier of Omissions, and those of Director of Remonstrance and Admonisher, established? Among these officials were men who remonstrated against enfeoffing the Director of Shanglin and concerning the splendor of Shanglin [?]; and men who remonstrated against an imperial hunting visit to Ganquan and requested the execution of sycophantic ministers. One declared that the reception of remonstrance fell short of that during the Zhenguan reign, and also remonstrated against a hunting expedition at Tongzhou. Another said that melons and fruit did not warrant the bestowal of office, and also blocked the white-hemp-paper edict appointing a chief minister. One firmly pressed his request that a military official deserved promotion for meritorious service. Another boldly insisted that an imperial command must not be altered, since it secured the trust of those below. A worthy man could not be retained; the man seeking to retain him cited his service in constructing the imperial mausoleum. An unwilling man [?] could not be dismissed; the man seeking his dismissal would not wait for the completion of his work on the imperial mausoleum. These were all men skilled in remonstrance who fulfilled their duties. Can you discuss them one by one?

We have also heard that remonstrance may be direct or indirect. To brave the ruler’s displeasure and touch the dragon’s forbidden scales, heedless of execution by having one’s heart cut out: this was the direct remonstrance of antiquity. In later ages, some who prided themselves on their frankness secretly supported wicked schemes and ingratiated themselves with treacherous men. The frankness of antiquity surely was not like this. To use subtle language and tactful expressions, conveying one’s meaning through the purport of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents: this was the indirect remonstrance of antiquity. In later ages, some who claimed a reputation for indirect remonstrance instead stirred thoughts of divine immortals and encouraged unrestrained indulgence in pleasure. The indirect remonstrance of antiquity surely was not like this.

Someone of former times said that the failings responsible for subordinates’ failure to remonstrate were ‘not three’ [?]. Can these failings indeed be eliminated? As for the methods of remonstrance…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
其術有五術果可用乎又有謂諫之道
有三難是固然矣臣子偕人之爵食人
之祿假處其難將以辭而止歟茲欲直
也不以爲訐諷也不以爲謏弊必去而
效忠術不用而見聽善處難諫之道求
合善諫之迹將何道而可諸士子抱藝
進取將欲有言願明以告我
問學必兼體以達用古之聖賢莫不皆
始以中州之士言之昔伊尹相商太公
===
興周體用之道備矣陳平濩嬰之輔漢
婁師德魏元忠之仕唐固皆一時之
然於明體之學果何如哉漢唐道學
明固亦莫之論也至於有宋人才盛出
或兄弟聯名俱以文章顯或兄弟並貴
俱以功業聞或三居言責數以論言去
或屢使虜庭卒以相業顯或正色立朝
而計安社稷或盡忠報國而幾復中原
是皆效用之臣者抑亦具立體之學歟
punctuated:
其術有五，術果可用乎？又有謂諫之道有三難，是固然矣。臣子偕人之爵，食人之祿，假處其難，將以辭而止歟？茲欲直也不以爲訐，諷也不以爲謏，弊必去而效忠，術不用而見聽，善處難諫之道，求合善諫之迹，將何道而可？諸士子抱藝進取，將欲有言，願明以告我。
問：學必兼體以達用，古之聖賢莫不皆始。以中州之士言之，昔伊尹相商，太公興周，體用之道備矣。陳平、濩嬰之輔漢，婁師德、魏元忠之仕唐，固皆一時之。然於明體之學，果何如哉？漢唐道學明，固亦莫之論也。至於有宋，人才盛出，或兄弟聯名，俱以文章顯；或兄弟並貴，俱以功業聞；或三居言責，數以論言去；或屢使虜庭，卒以相業顯；或正色立朝，而計安社稷；或盡忠報國，而幾復中原。是皆效用之臣者，抑亦具立體之學歟？
translation_en:
…There are five techniques: can these techniques indeed be employed? It is also said that the way of remonstrance presents three difficulties. This is certainly so. Yet ministers hold another’s rank [?] and eat another’s emoluments; if confronted with these difficulties, will they use them as an excuse to desist? Now, if one wishes to speak directly without being considered accusatory, to admonish indirectly without being considered a petty flatterer [?], surely to eliminate abuses and demonstrate loyalty, and to gain a hearing without employing techniques, how can one properly navigate the difficulties of remonstrance and accord with the examples of those skilled at it? You candidates bring your accomplishments in pursuit of advancement and will wish to speak out. Please explain this clearly to me.
Question: Learning must encompass underlying substance in order to attain practical application. The sages and worthies of antiquity all began with this [?]. Speaking of men from the Central Region, Yi Yin served as chief minister to the Shang, and Taigong brought the Zhou to ascendancy: in them the way of substance and application was complete. Chen Ping and Huo Ying [?] assisted the Han, while Lou Shide and Wei Yuanzhong served the Tang; all were certainly men of their age [text incomplete]. But what, in fact, was their learning concerning the elucidation of underlying substance? In the Han and Tang, learning of the Way was clear [?], yet indeed no one discussed it. Under the Song, talented men emerged in abundance. Some were brothers whose names were celebrated together, both distinguished for their literary compositions; some were brothers who both attained high rank and were renowned for their achievements. Some held remonstrance responsibilities three times and were repeatedly removed for their critical statements; some repeatedly went as envoys to the courts of the northern peoples and ultimately distinguished themselves through their achievements as chief ministers. Some stood at court with stern countenances and devised plans that secured the state; some served their country with utmost loyalty and came close to recovering the Central Plain. Were these all merely ministers who rendered effective service, or did they also possess the learning that establishes underlying substance?

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
至於明道伊川之伯仲則上接孔孟之
傳下開周程之統嗣道學之正明王道
之體而功業則實之兆也使試於用功
業亦可必乎亦可如諸公之盛乎先儒
謂其道同論一無復彼此故稱之則曰
程氏兩夫子述其言則合稱程子矣然
而又有謂明道似顏子伊川似孟子信
若斯言則是有異同矣又以明道似顏
子則絕類似伊川似孟下孟子大愚
===
非能及又若斯言則是有優劣也諸說
將何適從耶夫景行先哲固所當然審
所師尚尤為當務幸質論之以求體明
而用達也毋徒曰妄議先輩則吾豈敢
問刑為生殺人之具故有曰死者不可復
生斷者不可復續誠天下重事也以唐
虞盛世而猶設士師文武聖君而尚嘗
庶獄輔治弼教不可無刑而亦不可不
慎也古之刑官善者固有而惡者□□
punctuated:
至於明道、伊川之伯仲，則上接孔孟之傳，下開周程之統，嗣道學之正，明王道之體，而功業則實之兆也。使試於用，功業亦可必乎？亦可如諸公之盛乎？先儒謂其道同論一，無復彼此，故稱之則曰程氏兩夫子，述其言則合稱程子矣。然而又有謂明道似顏子，伊川似孟子。信若斯言，則是有異同矣。又以明道似顏子，則絕類似，伊川似孟下孟子大愚非能及。又若斯言，則是有優劣也。諸說將何適從耶？夫景行先哲，固所當然；審所師尚，尤為當務。幸質論之，以求體明而用達也。毋徒曰妄議先輩，則吾豈敢！

問：刑為生殺人之具，故有曰：「死者不可復生，斷者不可復續。」誠天下重事也。以唐虞盛世而猶設士師，文武聖君而尚嘗庶獄，輔治弼教，不可無刑，而亦不可不慎也。古之刑官，善者固有，而惡者□□
translation_en:
As for the brothers Mingdao and Yichuan, they carried forward the transmission of Confucius and Mencius from above and opened the succession of Zhou and Cheng below. They continued the orthodox learning of the Way and clarified the underlying substance of the Kingly Way, while practical achievements would signify its fruition. Had they been put to the test in office, could such achievements have been assured? Could they have matched the splendid accomplishments of the gentlemen mentioned earlier? Earlier Confucian scholars said that their Way was the same and their teachings one, with no further distinction between them. Thus they were called “the two Masters Cheng,” and when their sayings were recorded, both were referred to as “Master Cheng.” Yet others have said that Mingdao resembled Master Yan, and Yichuan resembled Mencius. If these words are true, there were differences as well as similarities. It is further said that Mingdao resembled Master Yan with an exceptionally close likeness [?], while Yichuan resembled Mencius; the following words, “below Mencius,” “great folly,” and “unable to attain,” are garbled [?]. If this statement is also true, there were differences in superiority and inferiority. Which of these views should we follow? Admiring the conduct of earlier sages is certainly proper; carefully determining whom to take as one’s teacher and esteem is an especially pressing task. Please examine and discuss this critically, seeking clarity in underlying substance and full realization in practical application. Do not merely say, “How could I dare presumptuously criticize my predecessors?”

Question: Punishments are instruments by which people are allowed to live or put to death. Hence it has been said: “The dead cannot be brought back to life, and severed limbs cannot be reattached.” This is truly a matter of the utmost gravity under Heaven. Even in the flourishing age of Tang and Yu, a Judge was appointed; even the sage kings Wen and Wu attended to the various legal cases [?]. To support government and assist moral instruction, punishments cannot be dispensed with, but neither can they be employed without care. Among the judicial officials of antiquity there were certainly good ones, while the bad ones [two illegible characters] …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
試與諸士爭評之爭辯孝婦而予雖封
侯其與斷獄三十年用法平恕而翕並
于公者同科爭救使臣而刑部如議其
與聽獄十二年天下稱頌而樹巢白鵲
者同撰錄因辯冤而貽母爲歡詣家勸
諭而感子成孝以言解兄弟爭田而致
其洒淚同居以恩感蠻夷獻馬而止受
一杯餞酒觀書屢嘆啓妻疑問而欲求
死獄之生實感殺辛驗可以直而不慢
===
拳右之禍此皆善爲法者也可得而
詳陳歟至若所愛者撓法活之所憎者
曲法滅之何偏私也其視巧排夫臣自
以爲功者伯仲耳捕奸連坐逮十餘家
論囚流血至數十里何殘刻也其視酷
爲鐵籠甚多誅殺者甲乙耳天資殘□
自比石勒而終有抉目摘肝之報屢□
制獄妄誅千人而竟招貿身殞命之□
與羅希奭推鞫詔獄相勉以虐而□□
punctuated:
試與諸士爭評之：爭辯孝婦，而予雖封侯，其與斷獄三十年、用法平恕而翕並于公者同科；爭救使臣，而刑部如議，其與聽獄十二年、天下稱頌而樹巢白鵲者同撰。錄因辯冤而貽母爲歡，詣家勸諭而感子成孝，以言解兄弟爭田而致其洒淚同居，以恩感蠻夷獻馬而止受一杯餞酒。觀書屢嘆，啓妻疑問，而欲求死獄之生；實感殺辛驗，可以直而不慢拳右之禍。此皆善爲法者也，可得而詳陳歟？
至若所愛者撓法活之，所憎者曲法滅之，何偏私也！其視巧排夫臣、自以爲功者，伯仲耳。捕奸連坐逮十餘家，論囚流血至數十里，何殘刻也！其視酷爲鐵籠、甚多誅殺者，甲乙耳。天資殘□，自比石勒，而終有抉目摘肝之報；屢□制獄，妄誅千人，而竟招貿身殞命之□；與羅希奭推鞫詔獄，相勉以虐，而□□
translation_en:
…Let us try to assess these men together with you candidates. The man who argued insistently in defense of a filial woman, with the words “although I am enfeoffed as a marquis” [?], belongs in the same category as the man who adjudicated cases for thirty years, applied the law impartially and leniently, and was ranked alongside Yu Gong [?]. The man who insistently sought to save an envoy, whose recommendation the Ministry of Justice accepted, belongs in the same class as the man who heard cases for twelve years, won praise throughout the realm, and had white magpies nest in his trees. There are accounts of a man who brought his mother joy by arguing against a wrongful accusation [?]; one who visited a household to offer counsel and persuaded a son to become filial; one who settled brothers’ dispute over fields through persuasion, bringing them to tears and inducing them to live together; and one whose kindness moved non-Chinese peoples to present horses, yet who accepted only a cup of farewell wine. One repeatedly sighed while reading documents, prompting his wife to question him, because he wished to find grounds for sparing those condemned to death. The passage about “killing Xin” and avoiding disaster from powerful men through uprightness without disrespect is unclear [?]. These were all men skilled in administering the law. Can you give a detailed account of them?
As for those who bent the law to preserve the lives of people they favored and twisted it to destroy those they hated—how partial they were! They were much of a kind with the man who cunningly drove out a great minister [?] and regarded this as an achievement. Arresting offenders, they implicated more than ten households through collective liability; sentencing prisoners, they caused blood to flow for scores of li. How cruel they were! They were on a par with the man who cruelly constructed iron cages and put great numbers to death. One, cruel by nature [illegible character], likened himself to Shi Le, but ultimately suffered the retribution of having his eyes gouged out and his liver torn out. Another repeatedly [illegible character] handled cases ordered by the emperor and wantonly executed a thousand people, but eventually brought upon himself [illegible character] the loss of his person and life [?]. Others investigated imperial prison cases with Luo Xishi, encouraging one another in brutality, and [two illegible characters]…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
之號播於當時希王安石職遷御史鍜
鍊城卒而羅織之名傳於當世數陷忠
良報施嗣續而與蔡京同傳誣致逗留
寃死父子而與秦檜同心此皆惡可為
戒者也可得而悉數歟諸士子抱藝賓
興駸駸嚮用他日或居內臺或在西部
或任郡邑而皆有刑名之詭善者可以
為法惡者可以為戒是必講之熟而見
之定矣請詳陳之毋讓□□□□□
===
其位
問水在天地間有利於國者莫如河有害
於民者亦莫如河河之為患惟豫為切
而豫之受害惟汴為先今歲霖潦連綿
河肆決溢延及四隄幾害城郭有志於
民者忍無計以處之乎夫水激而湍悍
者河之性也土卑而質疏者豫之地也
以是激而悍者乘彼卑而疏者其橫潰
之勢宜所必至不知大禹疏導之時河
punctuated:
之號播於當時。希王安石，職遷御史，鍜鍊城卒，而羅織之名傳於當世。數陷忠良，報施嗣續，而與蔡京同傳；誣致逗留，寃死父子，而與秦檜同心。此皆惡可為戒者也，可得而悉數歟？諸士子抱藝賓興，駸駸嚮用，他日或居內臺，或在西部，或任郡邑，而皆有刑名之詭。善者可以為法，惡者可以為戒，是必講之熟而見之定矣。請詳陳之，毋讓□□□□□其位。

問：水在天地間，有利於國者莫如河，有害於民者亦莫如河。河之為患，惟豫為切；而豫之受害，惟汴為先。今歲霖潦連綿，河肆決溢，延及四隄，幾害城郭。有志於民者，忍無計以處之乎？夫水激而湍悍者，河之性也；土卑而質疏者，豫之地也。以是激而悍者，乘彼卑而疏者，其橫潰之勢，宜所必至。不知大禹疏導之時，河
translation_en:
…the epithet spread in their own day. Another courted Wang Anshi’s favor and was promoted to Censor; by fabricating charges against the city guards, he acquired a contemporary reputation for weaving accusations. Another repeatedly brought down loyal and worthy men, with retribution visited upon his descendants, and shared a biography with Cai Jing. Another falsely charged men with delaying their advance, causing father and son to die unjustly, and was of one mind with Qin Hui. These are all examples of evil that can serve as warnings. Could they possibly be enumerated in full? You candidates, possessed of literary accomplishment and recommended through the Provincial Examination, are steadily approaching appointment. Some of you may one day serve in the Censorate, others in the western offices [?], and others in prefectural or county administrations; all will have responsibilities concerning penal matters [?]. The good can serve as models, and the evil as warnings. Surely you have studied these matters thoroughly and reached settled judgments. Please set them forth in detail, without deferring … [five illegible characters; the surviving conclusion, “his position,” is uncertain in context].

Question: Among the waters between Heaven and Earth, none benefits the state more than the Yellow River, and none does greater harm to the people. The troubles caused by the River are most acute in Yu, and within Yu, Bian suffers first and foremost. This year, prolonged rains and flooding have continued unabated. The River has broken its banks and overflowed unchecked, reaching the embankments on all four sides and nearly damaging the city walls. Could anyone devoted to the people bear to have no plan for dealing with this? Surging waters and a swift, violent current are the River’s nature; low terrain and loose soil characterize the land of Yu. When these surging, violent waters bear down upon that low, loose ground, widespread breaches are surely inevitable. We do not know whether, when the Great Yu dredged and channeled the waters, the River …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
水已經流於汴梁之地否歟或故道
失之後河水方改趨於洛汭之地否歟
夫大伾而下是謂大陸釃爲九渠合爲
一河以達於海此載於禹貢者甚明也
何緣今河反合渦河以達清淮而入於
海歟執古之陳迹以御今之更變亦何
不可而歷周漢以及宋元曾不得其要
妙歟我
朝建都北燕漕東南之粟以□京師〔□□〕
===
濟之境河之決也必不可使之□〔□□〕
決而東則漕渠乾涸綱運不通矣無論
民害如國計何茲欲處治得宜使無汎
濫衝溢之患其法何在前世言治河之
法有三曰疏曰濬曰塞何法爲長賈讓
之別有四曰生地曰故道曰河身曰減
水何說爲當賈讓之言三策嘗用於當
時否歟張商英之陳五事可用於今日
否歟尚文爲廉訪使曾陳治河大策未
punctuated: 水已經流於汴梁之地否歟？或故道失之後，河水方改趨於洛汭之地否歟？夫大伾而下，是謂大陸，釃爲九渠，合爲一河，以達於海，此載於《禹貢》者甚明也。何緣今河反合渦河，以達清淮而入於海歟？執古之陳迹，以御今之更變，亦何不可，而歷周漢以及宋元，曾不得其要妙歟？我朝建都北燕，漕東南之粟以□京師〔□□〕濟之境，河之決也，必不可使之□〔□□〕。決而東，則漕渠乾涸，綱運不通矣。無論民害，如國計何？茲欲處治得宜，使無汎濫衝溢之患，其法何在？前世言治河之法有三，曰疏，曰濬，曰塞，何法爲長？賈讓之別有四，曰生地，曰故道，曰河身，曰減水，何說爲當？賈讓之言三策，嘗用於當時否歟？張商英之陳五事，可用於今日否歟？尚文爲廉訪使，曾陳治河大策，未
translation_en:
…had the river already flowed through the territory of Bianliang? Or did its waters turn toward the confluence of the Luo only after its former course had been lost? Below Dapi lies what is called Dalu; the river divides into nine channels, then joins into a single river to reach the sea. This is recorded very clearly in the “Tribute of Yu.” Why, then, does the river now instead join the Guo River, reach the clear waters of the Huai, and enter the sea? What would be impossible about using the traces of ancient arrangements to manage present changes? Yet throughout the Zhou and Han, down to the Song and Yuan, was the essential solution never grasped?

Our dynasty established its capital in northern Yan and transports grain from the southeast by water to [illegible] the capital 〔two illegible characters〕. In the territory of Ji [?], when the river breaches its banks, it must never be allowed to [illegible] 〔two illegible characters〕. If it breaches eastward, the grain-transport canal will dry up and the transport fleets will be unable to pass. Quite apart from the harm to the people, what would become of the state's finances? If we now wish to manage it properly and avert flooding, destructive surges, and overflows, what method should we use?

Earlier generations spoke of three methods of controlling the river: opening channels, dredging, and blocking breaches. Which method is best? Jia Rang distinguished four categories: previously untouched land, the former course, the river channel itself, and reducing the flow. Which proposal is appropriate? Were the three policies proposed by Jia Rang ever put into practice in his own time? Could the five measures presented by Zhang Shangying be applied today? When Shang Wen served as Surveillance Commissioner, he once presented a comprehensive plan for controlling the river; it is not yet…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
知其陳於元者可以施於後歟賈魯爲
漕運使嘗陳治河二策未嘗其驗於彼
者可以施諸此歟以至宋濂作治河之
議丘濬亦有治河之論果折衷之已當
抑闕畧之未免歟諸士子窮經待用而
憂
國憂民之心宜素具也幸詳陳之以俟夫當
軸者採焉
punctuated: 知其陳於元者，可以施於後歟？賈魯爲漕運使，嘗陳治河二策，未嘗其驗於彼者，可以施諸此歟？以至宋濂作治河之議，丘濬亦有治河之論，果折衷之已當，抑闕畧之未免歟？諸士子窮經待用，而憂國憂民之心宜素具也。幸詳陳之，以俟夫當軸者採焉。
translation_en: …whether the proposals he presented under the Yuan can be applied in later times? When Jia Lu served as Commissioner of Grain Transport, he presented two plans for managing the Yellow River. Can what proved effective there be applied here [?]? Furthermore, Song Lian composed a discussion of river management, and Qiu Jun also wrote a discourse on it. Did they indeed arrive at sound judgments, or did omissions remain unavoidable? You candidates have thoroughly studied the Classics and await appointment; you should long have cultivated concern for the state and its people. Please set forth your views in detail, so that those directing affairs may draw upon them.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子於鄉黨恂恂如也似不能言者其在
宗廟朝廷便便言唯謹爾
李東熈
同考試官訓導郭　批〔揭書出題本平易要寫出聖人氣象自難此作獨能發之若親炙聖人者取冠本房無忝〕
同考試官學正李　批〔形容聖人千載宛然在目佳作也〕
===
考試官教授李　批〔分明畫出一箇聖人蓋必用心於學聖之工夫者欽杖起敬〕
考試官教授濮　批〔發揮盛德自中乎禮理明詞正僅見此篇〕
門人記聖人隨其所處之地而言貌有不同焉
蓋鄉黨廟朝地不同也則其言貌夫豈同哉聖
人德盛而周旋中禮有如是夫昔門人以孔子
之動靜無非至教故於其言貌無不謹書蓋曰

四書
