Anyone wishing to fulfill his responsibilities toward a household or a county must devote effort to these, and only thereafter proceed…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
遠之北寄生死之司欲扶之於至正稱之
於登平顧可於此有所歎哉噫風憲之職
難乎其盡矣論恩啓沃則在於忠誠彈壓
奸邪則在於剛勁廉察賢否則在於哲智
疏雪冤滯則在於欽恤是必有正大光明
之心忠厚詳慎之意而出之以公勤率之
以禮法然後能盡其職而不負於
國也洪惟我
朝
===
聖聖相承皆有製作以立言垂訓而
英宗睿皇帝憲綱一書則專爲風憲而設切切
于存心持身之戒歎列條示申命之不已
此居其位者所當究心也請陳之風憲之
設其來尚矣周官御史掌邦國都鄙萬民
之治令戰國秦趙澠池之會各命御史書
其事則職司紀載而不輕也審矣秦漢以
來以御史典糾察之任而所居之署或謂
之御史臺或謂之蘭臺寺或謂之憲臺或
punctuated:
遠之北，寄生死之司，欲扶之於至正，稱之於登平，顧可於此有所歎哉？噫！風憲之職，難乎其盡矣！論恩啓沃，則在於忠誠；彈壓奸邪，則在於剛勁；廉察賢否，則在於哲智；疏雪冤滯，則在於欽恤。是必有正大光明之心、忠厚詳慎之意，而出之以公勤，率之以禮法，然後能盡其職而不負於國也。
洪惟我朝，聖聖相承，皆有製作，以立言垂訓。而英宗睿皇帝《憲綱》一書，則專爲風憲而設，切切于存心持身之戒，歎列條示，申命之不已。此居其位者所當究心也。請陳之。
風憲之設，其來尚矣。《周官》，御史掌邦國都鄙萬民之治令。戰國秦趙澠池之會，各命御史書其事，則職司紀載而不輕也，審矣。秦漢以來，以御史典糾察之任，而所居之署，或謂之御史臺，或謂之蘭臺寺，或謂之憲臺，或
translation_en:
…the distant north [?], entrusted with authority over life and death: wishing to guide matters toward utmost rectitude and make them accord with an age of peace, could one have cause for lament in this regard [?]? Alas! How difficult it is to discharge the duties of censorial office fully! Discussing beneficence and enlightening the sovereign [?] requires loyalty and sincerity; suppressing the wicked and treacherous requires firmness and strength; investigating the worthy and unworthy requires discernment and wisdom; and redressing injustices and long-unresolved cases requires reverent care and compassion. One must possess an upright and open heart, with loyal, generous, attentive, and cautious intentions, expressing these through impartiality and diligence and guiding one’s conduct by ritual propriety and law. Only then can one fully discharge one’s duties without failing the state.
We reverently consider how, in our dynasty, sage sovereign has succeeded sage sovereign. All have composed works to establish enduring teachings and transmit instruction to posterity. The book Outline of Censorial Regulations (Xiangang), by Emperor Yingzong Rui, was written specifically for the censorial service. It insistently admonishes officials to preserve the proper disposition of mind and regulate their personal conduct, setting out instructions article by article [?] and reiterating its commands without cease. Those occupying these posts ought to study it earnestly. Allow me to explain.
The establishment of the censorial service dates back to antiquity. According to the Offices of Zhou, the censors were responsible for the governmental ordinances concerning the states, capitals, outlying districts, and all the people. At the meeting between Qin and Zhao at Mianchi during the Warring States period, each ruler ordered his censor to record the proceedings. It is thus clear that their office was charged with keeping records and was no minor responsibility. From the Qin and Han onward, censors were entrusted with investigating and impeaching misconduct. The office in which they served was variously called the Censorate (Yushi tai), the Orchid Terrace Office (Lantai si), the Censorial Terrace (Xiantai), or …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
謂之肅政臺名有不同而地無不要所任
之官有大夫有中丞有侍御史有監察御
史有御史裏行銜有不同而職無不當
時有若傅賢之執法蘭臺百僚敬服韋㒷
之執法殿中公卿畏憚武元衡之持平無
私而時君稱之杜衍之恩不假人而宰相
畏之皆在内之可稱者漢武帝遣直指使
者督郡國而不常置以後或遣博士或遣
侍御史唐貞觀初遣大使十三人巡省天
===
下以後分為二十道或十道或十五道道
各一使於是有按察採訪觀察處置司之
名宋開寶初遣常參官四人分詣諸路以
後諸路各置提點刑獄或以轉運使兼之
多寡不同或再周而罷或三年一奏久近
不一亦皆重之以耳目之任假之以風霜
之威當時有若綦勝之衣繡持斧出捕盜
賊韋允素繩糾吏治所至震慴馬亮之覆
訊冤獄全活甚多何明之作詩諭民强暴
punctuated:
謂之肅政臺，名有不同，而地無不要。所任之官，有大夫，有中丞，有侍御史，有監察御史，有御史裏行，銜有不同，而職無不當。時有若傅賢之執法蘭臺，百僚敬服；韋㒷之執法殿中，公卿畏憚；武元衡之持平無私，而時君稱之；杜衍之恩不假人，而宰相畏之，皆在内之可稱者。
漢武帝遣直指使者督郡國，而不常置，以後或遣博士，或遣侍御史。唐貞觀初，遣大使十三人巡省天下，以後分為二十道，或十道，或十五道，道各一使，於是有按察、採訪、觀察、處置司之名。宋開寶初，遣常參官四人分詣諸路，以後諸路各置提點刑獄，或以轉運使兼之。多寡不同，或再周而罷，或三年一奏，久近不一，亦皆重之以耳目之任，假之以風霜之威。當時有若綦勝之衣繡持斧，出捕盜賊；韋允素繩糾吏治，所至震慴；馬亮之覆訊冤獄，全活甚多；何明之作詩諭民，强暴
translation_en:
…or called the Office of Solemn Governance. Though their names differed, all occupied important positions. The officials appointed included Censors-in-chief, Vice Censors-in-chief, Attendant Censors, Investigating Censors, and Probationary Censors. Though their titles differed, each office had its appropriate duties. There were men such as Fu Xian [?], who enforced the law in the Orchid Terrace and won the respect and submission of all officials; Wei Xing [?], who enforced the law within the palace and was feared by the highest ministers; Wu Yuanheng, whose impartiality and freedom from private interests earned the reigning ruler’s praise; and Du Yan, who would not let others dispense favors in his name and was feared by the chief councilor. These were all praiseworthy examples among officials serving at the center.
Emperor Wu of Han dispatched Directly Appointed Emissaries to supervise the commanderies and kingdoms, but did not establish these as permanent posts. Subsequently, Erudites or Attendant Censors were sometimes dispatched. At the beginning of the Tang Zhenguan era, thirteen Grand Emissaries were sent to inspect the realm. Later it was divided into twenty circuits, or ten, or fifteen, with one emissary for each circuit. Thus arose offices bearing the names of Surveillance, Investigation, Observation, and Disposition. At the beginning of the Song Kaibao era, four officials who regularly attended court were sent separately to the various circuits. Later, each circuit was provided with a Judicial Commissioner, or a Transport Commissioner concurrently held that responsibility. Their numbers varied. Some appointments ended after two annual cycles, while others required a report every three years; their durations were not uniform. All, however, were entrusted with the weighty responsibility of serving as the ruler’s eyes and ears and invested with an authority as stern as wind and frost. Among them were Qi Sheng, who wore embroidered robes and carried an axe as he went out to arrest bandits; Wei Yunsu, who investigated and disciplined the administration of officials, inspiring fear wherever he went; Ma Liang, who reexamined cases of wrongful imprisonment and saved many lives; and He Ming, who composed poems to instruct the people, so that the violent and overbearing…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
知儆戒存于中而可稱者哉
國家稽古建官尤重風憲內設都察院十三
道外設十三按察司幷諸道署有常名員
有常額而非若前代之紛更于以使之總
察舉察于以使之典掌衆政白簡飛霜豪
强斂跡繡衣行部守令解綬
朝廷倚之以尊安邦國賴之以清肅職任之
重視昔有加
===
英宗睿皇帝慮居其位者之或敗度也爰述
列聖之意製爲憲綱一書俾遵守焉有曰風憲
存心須明白正大又曰風憲之官須存心
忠厚又曰居風憲者須持身端肅公勤詳
愼又曰行止語默必須循理守法進之以
向上之功本之以檢身之學蓋欲其戒奸
回之私袪刻薄之行而純其心以出政端
其本以率物非徒隆之以雄峻之勢尊之
以崇待之班也當其事者苟不盡誠於身
心之學幾何不爲
punctuated:
知儆戒，存于中而可稱者哉？

國家稽古建官，尤重風憲。內設都察院十三道，外設十三按察司幷諸道，署有常名，員有常額，而非若前代之紛更。于以使之總察舉察，于以使之典掌衆政。白簡飛霜，豪强斂跡；繡衣行部，守令解綬。朝廷倚之以尊安，邦國賴之以清肅，職任之重，視昔有加。

英宗睿皇帝慮居其位者之或敗度也，爰述列聖之意，製爲《憲綱》一書，俾遵守焉。有曰：「風憲存心須明白正大。」又曰：「風憲之官須存心忠厚。」又曰：「居風憲者須持身端肅，公勤詳愼。」又曰：「行止語默，必須循理守法。」進之以向上之功，本之以檢身之學，蓋欲其戒奸回之私，袪刻薄之行，而純其心以出政，端其本以率物，非徒隆之以雄峻之勢，尊之以崇待之班也。當其事者苟不盡誠於身心之學，幾何不爲
translation_en:
…came to heed the warning—were these deeds retained in memory and worthy of praise [?]?

In establishing offices after ancient precedents, our dynasty has placed particular weight on censorial oversight. At the center it has established the Censorate with its thirteen circuits; outside the capital, thirteen Provincial Surveillance Commissions together with their subordinate circuits. Offices have fixed names and their personnel fixed quotas, unlike the incessant changes of earlier dynasties. These officials are charged with comprehensive scrutiny and inspection [?], and with overseeing the many affairs of government. When their white impeachment tablets send frost flying, powerful bullies conceal their activities; when the embroidered-robed censors tour their jurisdictions, prefects and magistrates lay aside their seals of office. The court relies upon them for its dignity and security, and the realm depends upon them for purity and order. The importance of their responsibilities exceeds that of former times.

Emperor Yingzong Rui, concerned that those occupying these posts might violate the established standards, accordingly carried forward the intentions of his imperial predecessors and compiled a book, the Censorial Regulations (Xiangang), for them to observe. It states: “Those exercising censorial oversight must keep their minds clear, upright, and magnanimous.” It also states: “Censorial officials must cherish loyalty and generosity.” Again: “Those holding censorial office must conduct themselves with propriety and gravity, impartiality and diligence, thoroughness and caution.” Again: “In action and repose, speech and silence, they must follow principle and observe the law.” He sought to advance them through efforts toward higher attainment and to ground them in the learning of self-discipline. His intention was surely that they guard against treacherous private motives, cast off harsh and ungenerous conduct, purify their minds in issuing measures of government, and rectify their own foundations so as to lead others. He did not merely exalt them with formidable authority and honor them with an elevated station. If those entrusted with these duties fail to devote themselves sincerely to cultivating their persons and minds, how could they avoid…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖訓之孤哉哉然漢唐以後能無媿於身心者寡
過於周程二子故程子為御史裏行則以
拾遺補闕為己任使得久於其職格非之
功大矣周子為提點刑獄則以洗冤澤民
為己任使得竟其所施及物之功溥矣今
日秉憲之士類皆鍊達之人其於
聖訓講之有素佩之無遺孰專謂職當務之
急尚多未洗之冤亦春秋責備之義也蓋
君子饑渴民隱急務敢略蹤邑囊以達
===
形庭者何者非輔世之良圖其未敢陳者恐
亦細故耳籍寃下生寃獄敢忘乏星軺以
馳亦縣者何者非救民之至論其未敢辯
者恐為疑獄耳又謂
聖訓所在體之而未至持之而欠誠未必其無
而方圖自勉其云拘於勢而限於力風憲
不有也雖然風憲責人者也人亦得而責
之居其位而有所不知知之而有所不行
行之而君子病焉小人幸焉風憲之責也
punctuated:
聖訓之孤哉哉！然漢唐以後，能無媿於身心者，寡過於周程二子。故程子為御史裏行，則以拾遺補闕為己任；使得久於其職，格非之功大矣。周子為提點刑獄，則以洗冤澤民為己任；使得竟其所施，及物之功溥矣。
今日秉憲之士，類皆鍊達之人，其於聖訓，講之有素，佩之無遺。孰專謂職當務之急，尚多未洗之冤，亦春秋責備之義也。蓋君子饑渴民隱，急務敢略蹤邑囊以達形庭者，何者非輔世之良圖？其未敢陳者，恐亦細故耳。籍寃下生寃獄，敢忘乏星軺以馳亦縣者，何者非救民之至論？其未敢辯者，恐為疑獄耳。
又謂聖訓所在，體之而未至，持之而欠誠，未必其無，而方圖自勉。其云拘於勢而限於力，風憲不有也。雖然，風憲責人者也，人亦得而責之。居其位而有所不知，知之而有所不行，行之而君子病焉、小人幸焉，風憲之責也。
translation_en:
…would they not betray the imperial instructions! Yet since the Han and Tang, few whose cultivation of person and mind was beyond reproach have surpassed the two masters, Zhou and Cheng. Thus, when Master Cheng served as a censor on probation, he took it upon himself to remedy omissions and deficiencies. Had he been able to remain long in office, his achievements in correcting wrongdoing would have been great. When Master Zhou served as judicial commissioner, he took it upon himself to redress injustices and benefit the people. Had he been able to carry his measures through, their benefits would have extended widely.
Those who wield censorial authority today are generally experienced and discerning men. They have long studied the imperial instructions and treasure them without omission. To say that urgent official duties still leave many injustices unredressed [?] also accords with the principle of demanding the fullest performance of duty found in the Spring and Autumn Annals. The gentleman is as eager to address the people's hidden sufferings as a hungry or thirsty person is for food or drink. As for urgent matters conveyed to the court [?; the wording here is garbled], which proposals are not sound plans for assisting the age? Those they have not ventured to present are perhaps only minor matters. As for records of injustice, wrongful prosecutions, and journeys by an envoy's carriage to the counties [?; the wording here is garbled], which arguments are not of the utmost importance for saving the people? Those cases they have not ventured to contest are perhaps doubtful ones.
It is further said that, in following the imperial instructions, some may fall short in putting them into practice or lack sincerity in upholding them. Such shortcomings may indeed exist, while those concerned are seeking to spur themselves onward. But the claim that circumstances constrain them and their powers limit them has no place among censorial officials. Nevertheless, censorial officials call others to account, and others may likewise call them to account. To hold such office yet leave matters unknown; to know of them yet fail to act; or to act in ways that distress gentlemen and delight petty men—these are failings for which censorial officials must answer.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
風憲縱不能自昔如天下之人何敢以此
爲司風憲者告
第二問
宋汝灜
同考試官教諭孟　批〔於鋪敘之間而有抑揚低昂家數善於策者〕
同考試官教諭毛　批〔類能荅之而筆力強勁吾惟得之於予也當刻〕
考試官教授李　批〔不拘問目間新意以〕
===
飾故實可嘉
考試官教授濮　批〔有考據有議論〕
論諫諍之法於三代之前似疎而實密論
諫諍之法於三代之後似密而實疎而大
要皆以忠誠爲之本也蓋忠誠則直言而
君不以爲訐諷言而君不以爲譏可以引
君於當道可以納君於無過而彼三難三
弊五術之說有不必論矣不然則雖進萬
言殞九首尚何益諫君之職而成諫君之
punctuated:
風憲縱不能自昔，如天下之人何？敢以此爲司風憲者告。

第二問
宋汝灜
同考試官教諭孟，批〔於鋪敘之間而有抑揚低昂家數，善於策者。〕
同考試官教諭毛，批〔類能荅之，而筆力強勁。吾惟得之於予也，當刻。〕
考試官教授李，批〔不拘問目，間新意以〕飾故實，可嘉。
考試官教授濮，批〔有考據，有議論。〕

論諫諍之法於三代之前，似疎而實密；論諫諍之法於三代之後，似密而實疎。而大要皆以忠誠爲之本也。蓋忠誠則直言而君不以爲訐，諷言而君不以爲譏，可以引君於當道，可以納君於無過，而彼三難、三弊、五術之說，有不必論矣。不然，則雖進萬言，殞九首，尚何益諫君之職，而成諫君之
translation_en:
…Even if the censorial authorities cannot themselves [act as in former times?], how can they answer to the people of the realm? I venture to offer these words to those charged with censorial duties.

Second Policy Question
Song Ruying 宋汝灜

Associate Examiner Meng, Instructor, comments: “Within the exposition there is a practiced command of emphasis and modulation: this is someone skilled in policy essays.”
Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “He answers virtually all the points, and his writing is vigorous. I alone have obtained this in you [?]. It should be printed.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “He is not confined by the question’s specific headings, but intersperses fresh ideas to embellish historical precedents. Commendable.”
Examiner Pu, Professor, comments: “There is evidential research, and there is reasoned argument.”

Considering the methods of remonstrance before the Three Dynasties, they appear lax but are actually thorough; considering the methods of remonstrance after the Three Dynasties, they appear thorough but are actually lax. Yet their essential foundation in every case is loyalty and sincerity. With loyalty and sincerity, one may speak directly without the ruler taking it as an accusation, and speak through allusion without the ruler taking it as mockery. One can lead the ruler onto the proper path and bring him to freedom from error. There is then no need to discuss those theories of the three difficulties, the three failings, and the five techniques. Otherwise, even if one submits ten thousand words and loses nine heads, how could this help fulfill the duty of remonstrating with the ruler and achieve the …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
功哉傳曰勿欺也而犯之又曰君子信而
後諫未信則以爲謗己也勿欺而信其忠
誠之謂乎慨昔唐虞三代之時君以納諫
爲明臣以進諫爲良内自臣工外及庶氏
皆可言之人無常員也若箴若頌若議若
謗皆可盡之言無時諱也故德澤不至壅
於下流奸邪不至蔽於上聽猗歟盛哉自
漢孝武置大夫光武改諫議大夫而諫官
有定職唐置拾遺補闕宋置司諫正言而
===
諫官有常員如是而欲聰明無所遺政事
無所失得乎然其間有職於諫而不敢不
言有不職於諫而不能自默故有若張釋
之諫封上林之令東方朔諫殺上林之鹿
欲獵甘泉薛廣德謂關東困極以阻其行
尊禮張禹朱雲願借劍尚方以誅佞臣是
皆諫之各於漢也又若魏徵諫悟太宗不
及貞觀之初劉仁軌諫止太宗校獵同州
之舉欲官獻以羣而陸贄力言公器不可
punctuated: 功哉？傳曰：「勿欺也，而犯之。」又曰：「君子信而後諫，未信則以爲謗己也。」勿欺而信，其忠誠之謂乎！慨昔唐虞三代之時，君以納諫爲明，臣以進諫爲良，内自臣工，外及庶氏，皆可言之，人無常員也；若箴，若頌，若議，若謗，皆可盡之，言無時諱也。故德澤不至壅於下流，奸邪不至蔽於上聽，猗歟盛哉！自漢孝武置大夫，光武改諫議大夫，而諫官有定職；唐置拾遺、補闕，宋置司諫、正言，而諫官有常員。如是而欲聰明無所遺，政事無所失，得乎？然其間有職於諫而不敢不言，有不職於諫而不能自默。故有若張釋之諫封上林之令，東方朔諫殺上林之鹿；欲獵甘泉，薛廣德謂關東困極以阻其行；尊禮張禹，朱雲願借劍尚方以誅佞臣。是皆諫之各於漢也。又若魏徵諫悟太宗不及貞觀之初，劉仁軌諫止太宗校獵同州之舉；欲官獻以羣，而陸贄力言公器不可
translation_en:
…accomplish the purpose of remonstrating with the ruler? The transmitted text says, “Do not deceive him, but confront him.” It also says, “The gentleman remonstrates only after gaining trust. Without that trust, the ruler will regard him as slandering himself.” Not deceiving and being trusted—does this not mean loyalty and sincerity?

We look back with longing to the age of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, when rulers regarded accepting remonstrance as enlightened, and ministers regarded offering it as worthy. From officials within the court to ordinary people outside it, all could speak: those who spoke were not a fixed body of personnel. Admonitions, praises, discussions, and criticisms—all could be fully expressed, with no occasion on which speech was taboo. Thus the benefits of virtuous rule were not blocked from flowing down to those below, nor could treacherous men obstruct what reached the ruler’s ears. Ah, how flourishing an age!

After Emperor Xiaowu of Han established Grand Masters, and Emperor Guangwu changed their title to Grand Masters of Remonstrance, remonstrance officials had designated duties. The Tang established Reminders and Rectifiers of Omissions; the Song established Remonstrators, styled sijian and zhengyan. Remonstrance officials thus became a fixed body of personnel. Under such arrangements, could one expect the ruler’s perception to overlook nothing and the conduct of government to be free from error?

Yet among them were men charged with remonstrance who dared not remain silent, and others without that charge who could not keep silent. Thus Zhang Shizhi remonstrated against ennobling the director of Shanglin, and Dongfang Shuo remonstrated over the killing of a deer in Shanglin. When the emperor wished to hunt at Ganquan, Xue Guangde cited the extreme distress of the region east of the passes to prevent his journey. When the emperor treated Zhang Yu with honor and ceremony, Zhu Yun asked to borrow a sword from the Imperial Manufactories to execute the sycophantic minister. These were all examples of remonstrance under the Han [?].

Likewise, Wei Zheng’s remonstrance brought Emperor Taizong to recognize that he fell short of his conduct at the beginning of the Zhenguan era. Liu Rengui’s remonstrance stopped Taizong’s proposed hunting expedition to Tongzhou. When the emperor wished to confer office for an offering of a herd [?], Lu Zhi forcefully declared that the public instruments of authority must not…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
輕欲相裴延齡而陽城欲壞白麻以慟哭
是皆諫之名於唐也至若武臣有功當封
太祖堅執終可其奏者趙普也命令不可
屢更仁宗感悟卒納其言者尹洙也蔡襄
之君子英宗欲去之傅堯俞謂其有山陵
之功而不能去高居簡之小人皆欲留
之司馬光謂其不待山陵之功而不能留
是又宋之名能諫者然又聞諸孔子曰有
直諫有諷諫以直諫言之龍逢比干之犯
===
顏逆鱗不顧剖心之誅至今生氣凜然後
世若谷永之越職抗議劉棲楚之叩頭死
爭似慷慨矣或陰為黨王氏之謀或黨裴欲
附逢吉之意直如此乎羞是者非直之病
諫乃諫者之未效於直也以諷諫言之傳
說周公之微言婉辭託意詩書之旨至今
高風宛然後世若相如子虛之賦子雲羽
獵之賦似委曲矣或適啓神仙之想或反
滋遊樂之心爾苦是乎若是者非諷之病
punctuated: 輕；欲相裴延齡，而陽城欲壞白麻以慟哭，是皆諫之名於唐也。至若武臣有功當封，太祖堅執，終可其奏者，趙普也；命令不可屢更，仁宗感悟，卒納其言者，尹洙也。蔡襄之君子，英宗欲去之，傅堯俞謂其有山陵之功，而不能去；高居簡之小人，皆欲留之，司馬光謂其不待山陵之功，而不能留。是又宋之名能諫者。然又聞諸孔子曰：「有直諫，有諷諫。」以直諫言之，龍逢、比干之犯顏逆鱗，不顧剖心之誅，至今生氣凜然。後世若谷永之越職抗議、劉棲楚之叩頭死爭，似慷慨矣；或陰為黨王氏之謀，或黨裴欲附逢吉之意。直如此乎？羞是者，非直之病諫，乃諫者之未效於直也。以諷諫言之，傳說、周公之微言婉辭，託意詩書之旨，至今高風宛然。後世若相如《子虛》之賦、子雲《羽獵》之賦，似委曲矣；或適啓神仙之想，或反滋遊樂之心。爾苦是乎？若是者，非諷之病
translation_en:
…be treated lightly. When the emperor wished to appoint Pei Yanling chief councillor, Yang Cheng proposed tearing up the appointment edict on white hemp paper and weeping bitterly. These were all men renowned for remonstrance under the Tang. As for the Song, when a military official had earned enfeoffment through his service and Emperor Taizu stubbornly resisted, it was Zhao Pu whose petition he ultimately approved. When Emperor Renzong was moved to recognize that commands must not be repeatedly changed and finally accepted this counsel, it was Yin Zhu who had offered it. Emperor Yingzong wished to dismiss the gentleman Cai Xiang, but Fu Yaoyu said that Cai had rendered service in connection with the imperial mausoleum, and he could not be dismissed. All wished to retain the petty man Gao Jujian [?], but Sima Guang said that one need not wait for him to render service in connection with the imperial mausoleum, and he could not be retained. These, too, were Song men renowned for their ability to remonstrate.
Yet I have also heard these words attributed to Confucius: “There is direct remonstrance, and there is indirect remonstrance.” Speaking of direct remonstrance, Long Feng and Bi Gan braved their rulers’ anger and touched the dragon’s forbidden scale, heedless of the punishment of having their hearts cut out. To this day their vital spirit inspires awe. In later ages, Gu Yong went beyond his official duties to protest, and Liu Qichu struck his head against the ground, disputing at the risk of death: they seem to have been impassioned and courageous. Yet one secretly plotted to support the Wang clan, while the other sided with Pei with the intention of attaching himself to Fengji. Is this what it means to be forthright? In such cases [?], it is not forthrightness that impairs remonstrance; rather, those remonstrating have failed to achieve true forthrightness.
Speaking of indirect remonstrance, Fu Yue [?] and the Duke of Zhou used subtle words and gentle expressions, entrusting their intentions to the import of the Odes and the Documents. Their lofty example remains vividly present to this day. In later ages, Xiangru’s “Rhapsody on Master Zixu” and Ziyun’s “Rhapsody on the Feathered Hunt” seem to have been tactfully indirect. Yet one merely awakened thoughts of immortals, while the other instead nourished a desire for excursions and pleasure. Is this how it should be [?]? In such cases, it is not indirectness that impairs …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
諫乃諫者之不得於諷也陸贄謂下之不
諫其弊有三謟諛者順旨而忠實之旨不
聞顧望者自便而切磋之詞不盡畏懦者
避辜而情理之說不申仗馬不鳴首鼠自
默其弊誠有也至若蘇洵謂遊說之術可
法於諫者五理諭之勢禁之利誘之激怒
之隱諷之是也然以忠誠自盡爲慮者矣
彼遊說之士或可以機智勇辯濟其詐進
諫之人則難以機智勇辯濟其忠若此五
===
術可使法於諫乎呂伯恭謂諫諍之道難
於爲言者三遠則情不接疎則情不親驟
則理不究固也然欲勢近情親見數言漸
則可諫之人少不可諫之人多可諫之時
少不可諫之時多畏此三難可遂廢其諫
乎姑因明問所及如此然竊有說焉漢唐
宋之諫者雖當時有名執事謂皆善諫而
盡職否也顧其心術不能無純疵之殊而
行事未免有淺慮之異特取其一時一事
punctuated: 諫，乃諫者之不得於諷也。陸贄謂下之不諫，其弊有三：謟諛者順旨，而忠實之旨不聞；顧望者自便，而切磋之詞不盡；畏懦者避辜，而情理之說不申。仗馬不鳴，首鼠自默，其弊誠有也。至若蘇洵謂遊說之術可法於諫者五：理諭之，勢禁之，利誘之，激怒之，隱諷之，是也。然以忠誠自盡爲慮者矣。彼遊說之士，或可以機智勇辯濟其詐；進諫之人，則難以機智勇辯濟其忠。若此五術，可使法於諫乎？呂伯恭謂諫諍之道難於爲言者三：遠則情不接，疎則情不親，驟則理不究。固也。然欲勢近情親，見數言漸，則可諫之人少，不可諫之人多；可諫之時少，不可諫之時多。畏此三難，可遂廢其諫乎？姑因明問所及如此。然竊有說焉：漢唐宋之諫者，雖當時有名，執事謂皆善諫而盡職否也？顧其心術，不能無純疵之殊；而行事，未免有淺慮之異。特取其一時一事
translation_en:
…remonstrance; rather, the remonstrators failed to master indirect admonition. Lu Zhi said that when subordinates fail to remonstrate, three evils arise: flatterers comply with the ruler’s wishes, so that loyal and honest intentions go unheard; those who hesitate and watch for advantage seek their own convenience, so that words of mutual correction are not fully expressed; and the timid avoid blame, so that arguments grounded in circumstances and principle are not set forth. Like horses in the ceremonial guard that do not neigh, they waver and remain silent. These evils certainly exist.

As for Su Xun’s assertion that five techniques of persuasion may serve as models for remonstrance, these are: convincing through reason, restraining through the force of circumstances, enticing through advantage, provoking anger, and admonishing obliquely. Yet these give cause for concern to those who would devote themselves fully in loyalty and sincerity [?]. Persuaders may use ingenuity, boldness, and eloquence to carry through their deception; those who offer remonstrance can hardly use ingenuity, boldness, and eloquence to fulfill their loyalty. Can these five techniques, then, be taken as models for remonstrance?

Lü Bogong said that three circumstances make it difficult to speak in remonstrance: when one is distant, feelings do not communicate; when one lacks intimacy, feelings are not close; and when one speaks abruptly, principles are not fully explored. This is certainly so. Yet if one requires proximity in position, intimacy of feeling, frequent audiences, and a gradual approach in speaking, there will be few people able to remonstrate and many unable to do so, few occasions when remonstrance is possible and many when it is not. May one abandon remonstrance altogether out of fear of these three difficulties?

For now, I have responded thus to the matters raised in your discerning question. Yet I venture to add a further observation. Although the remonstrators of the Han, Tang, and Song were renowned in their own times, would you, sir, say that they all remonstrated well and fully discharged their duties? Looking at their intentions, there were inevitably differences of purity and blemish; in their conduct, too, there were differences in shallow deliberation [?]. If we take only their words on a particular occasion concerning a particular matter…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
之言亦皆愛君愛國之意可矣若論其極
則豈無可議哉士君子僭人之爵而食人
之祿寄之以諫之職而責之以諫之任幸
而當諷諫之時必以傳說周公為法而當
盡納約自牖之道不幸而居直諫之地必
以龍逢比干為法而務竭披肝露膽之心
盡忠誠於直諫而□□諷盡忠誠於
諷諫而使□□□也陸贄之所謂弊
全無患□□□□□□□誠焉具見其弊哉
===
呂伯恭之所謂難於盡忠誠者也苟盡忠
誠焉何有於難哉惟忠貫日月雖驟亦容
有易從之理至誠動天地雖疏亦容有可
入之幾而彼蘇洵之所謂術者正不可用
且不必用而亦不能用也管見如斯倘與
其進而有言責或直或諷動法前哲庶幾
洪範宋諸君子之往迹亦不必求其皆合
也執事以為何如
第三問
punctuated:
之言，亦皆愛君愛國之意，可矣。若論其極，則豈無可議哉？士君子僭人之爵而食人之祿，寄之以諫之職而責之以諫之任，幸而當諷諫之時，必以傳說、周公為法，而當盡納約自牖之道；不幸而居直諫之地，必以龍逢、比干為法，而務竭披肝露膽之心。盡忠誠於直諫而□□諷，盡忠誠於諷諫而使□□□也。陸贄之所謂弊，全無患□□□□□□□誠焉，具見其弊哉？呂伯恭之所謂難於盡忠誠者也。苟盡忠誠焉，何有於難哉？惟忠貫日月，雖驟亦容有易從之理；至誠動天地，雖疏亦容有可入之幾。而彼蘇洵之所謂術者，正不可用，且不必用，而亦不能用也。管見如斯，倘與其進而有言責，或直或諷，動法前哲，庶幾洪範宋諸君子之往迹，亦不必求其皆合也。執事以為何如？
第三問。
translation_en:
…their words may indeed all be accepted as expressions of love for their ruler and their country. Yet if we examine them to the utmost, could there be nothing open to criticism? A gentleman who presumptuously occupies another’s rank and draws another’s stipend, entrusted with the office of remonstrance and charged with its responsibilities, must, if fortunate enough to encounter a time suited to indirect remonstrance, take Fu Yue [?] (傳說) and the Duke of Zhou as his models, fully pursuing the way of “presenting simple offerings through the window”—approaching the ruler through an opening to his understanding. If, less fortunately, he finds himself in circumstances requiring direct remonstrance, he must take Long Feng and Bi Gan as his models and strive to lay bare his heart with complete sincerity. He must devote his utmost loyalty and sincerity to direct remonstrance and … indirect remonstrance [?]; he must devote his utmost loyalty and sincerity to indirect remonstrance and cause … [?]. As for what Lu Zhi called its defects, “entirely without trouble” … sincerity … would its defects all be evident [?]?
This is what Lü Bogong called the difficulty of giving full expression to loyalty and sincerity. If one gives full expression to loyalty and sincerity, what difficulty is there? Loyalty penetrates the sun and moon: even when advice is offered abruptly, there may still be grounds for its ready acceptance. Perfect sincerity moves Heaven and Earth: even when the relationship is distant, there may still be an opening through which advice can enter. As for what Su Xun called techniques, these are precisely what ought not to be used; indeed, there is no need to use them, nor can they be used.
Such is my limited view. Should I be permitted to advance into office and bear responsibility for speaking out, whether directly or indirectly, I would in every action model myself on the worthy men of the past. I might thereby approach … the past deeds of the gentlemen of the Song [?]; nor need I seek to conform to them in every respect. What do you think, sir?
Third question.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
何景明
同考試官訓導林　批　此盖素有講明而
發之於詞渾融可愛非若他人之東牽西補
以塞問目者
同考試官教諭王　批　議論切當而末以
伊尹太公自期待若命古者
考試官教授李　批　前二塲俱優而此塲
稱是當置前焉
考試官教授濮　批　援引詳明而歸宿至
當盖有學之士也合寘本房
===
體立而用行也行著於用者知其體之立
體具而用周也故備其體者知其用之全
然體之立也有偏全則用之見也有純疵
時之濟也有違合則用之見也有大小知
其體之全者固可必其用之大見其用之
大者豈盡信其體之明乎夫聖學大明講
論有素則士知全體之學而功之盛者固
得之學問也乞學雖無傳質乃純粹則
punctuated:
何景明

同考試官訓導林批：此盖素有講明，而發之於詞，渾融可愛，非若他人之東牽西補以塞問目者。

同考試官教諭王批：議論切當，而末以伊尹、太公自期待，若命古者。

考試官教授李批：前二塲俱優，而此塲稱是，當置前焉。

考試官教授濮批：援引詳明，而歸宿至當，盖有學之士也，合寘本房。

體立而用行也，行著於用者，知其體之立。體具而用周也，故備其體者，知其用之全。然體之立也有偏全，則用之見也有純疵；時之濟也有違合，則用之見也有大小。知其體之全者，固可必其用之大；見其用之大者，豈盡信其體之明乎？夫聖學大明，講論有素，則士知全體之學，而功之盛者，固得之學問也。乞學雖無傳，質乃純粹，則
translation_en:
He Jingming

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: This evidently comes from sustained study and clarification. Expressed in words, it forms a harmonious and pleasing whole, unlike others’ attempts to cobble together material from here and there merely to fill out answers to the questions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The argument is apt and sound. At the end, he sets himself the ambition of emulating Yi Yin and Taigong, as though taking the men of antiquity as his charge [?].

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: His work in the first two sessions was excellent, and this session’s work matches it. He should be ranked near the top.

Comment by Examiner Pu, Professor: His citations are detailed and clear, and his conclusions entirely appropriate. He is evidently a man of learning and should be placed in this examination section.

When substance is established, function operates; where conduct manifests itself in function, one knows that its substance is established. When substance is complete, function is comprehensive; thus, where substance is fully present, one knows that function is complete. Yet substance may be established partially or fully, and its manifestation in function consequently has purity or flaws. Success in meeting the circumstances of the times may encounter adverse or favorable conditions, and function consequently manifests itself on a greater or smaller scale. Knowing that someone’s substance is complete, one may indeed be certain that his function will be great; but, seeing the greatness of his function, can one be entirely confident that his substance is clearly understood? When the learning of the sages shines brightly and has long been expounded and discussed, scholars understand learning that embraces the whole substance; their splendid achievements are assuredly attained through study. Though learning may lack transmission [?], if one’s natural endowment is pure, then…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
士有一得之者而功之成者成於天資之
美古之君子莫不皆然豈獨中州之士哉
然中州之士愚生願仰望以爲約從者也
敢因明問所及而言之三代以上道學之
明故伊尹肖君臣一德之美而輔商之功
以成太公有丹書敬義之戒而興周之業
以著漢唐以來此學不講陳平張嬰功業
之建於漢者固亦奚而所以得此者天資
之美耳要其學雖文如賈誼者且未知之
===
何暇他及乎況師德魏元忠忠藎之竭於
唐者固至矣而所以得此者亦天資之美
耳論其學雖文如韓愈者且未之豈望其
他求乎五星兆祥於奎期之昌於宋然
不登濂洛之門則才雖大道之要其間有
若宋祁宋庠兄弟皆以文章顯著述之美
近於知道者而不純韓絳韓維伯仲皆以
相業開建明之大邇於立體者而未全呂
誨之三居言責論糾大臣之得失屢黜
punctuated: 士有一得之者，而功之成者，成於天資之美。古之君子莫不皆然，豈獨中州之士哉？然中州之士，愚生願仰望以爲約從者也。敢因明問所及而言之。三代以上，道學之明，故伊尹肖君臣一德之美，而輔商之功以成；太公有丹書敬義之戒，而興周之業以著。漢唐以來，此學不講，陳平、張嬰功業之建於漢者，固亦奚，而所以得此者，天資之美耳。要其學，雖文如賈誼者，且未知之，何暇他及乎？況師德、魏元忠忠藎之竭於唐者，固至矣，而所以得此者，亦天資之美耳。論其學，雖文如韓愈者，且未之，豈望其他求乎？五星兆祥於奎，期之昌於宋。然不登濂洛之門，則才雖大道之要，其間有若宋祁、宋庠兄弟，皆以文章顯，著述之美，近於知道者而不純；韓絳、韓維伯仲，皆以相業開，建明之大，邇於立體者而未全；呂誨之三居言責，論糾大臣之得失，屢黜。
translation_en:
…among scholars, some grasp a single aspect of it, and their accomplishments arise from the excellence of their natural endowments. This was true of all the gentlemen of antiquity; how could it be true only of the scholars of the Central Plain? Yet the scholars of the Central Plain are those whom I, an unworthy student, wish to look up to and join in fellowship. I venture to speak of them in response to your discerning question.
In the Three Dynasties and earlier, learning of the Way was clearly understood. Thus Yi Yin exemplified [?] the excellence of ruler and minister sharing one virtue, and accomplished his work of assisting the Shang. The Grand Duke possessed the admonition concerning reverence and righteousness in the Cinnabar Writ (Danshu), and his achievement in establishing the Zhou became manifest. From the Han and Tang onward, this learning was no longer expounded. The achievements established under the Han by Chen Ping and Zhang Ying [?] were indeed also [text unclear], but what enabled them to achieve these things was simply the excellence of their natural endowments. As for this learning, even someone as accomplished in letters as Jia Yi did not yet understand it. How could others have had leisure to attain it?
Moreover, Shide and Wei Yuanzhong carried their loyal service to the Tang to the utmost; yet what enabled them to do so was likewise simply the excellence of their natural endowments. As for their learning, even someone as accomplished in letters as Han Yu had not yet [grasped] it [?]; how could one expect others to seek it?
The five planets portended good fortune in the Kui constellation, heralding its flourishing under the Song [?]. Yet without entering the school of Lian and Luo, even great talent [could not grasp] the essentials of the Way [?]. Among these men were the brothers Song Qi and Song Xiang, both renowned for their literary compositions. The excellence of their writings approached an understanding of the Way, but was not pure. The brothers Han Jiang and Han Wei both distinguished themselves through their achievements as chief councillors [?]. The greatness of the proposals they advanced approached the establishment of the fundamental substance, but was not complete. Lü Hui thrice held office charged with remonstrance, discussing and censuring the merits and faults of high ministers, and was repeatedly dismissed…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
無所悔嘗彌之屢役屢黜以身繫天下之
安危去就無所累雖其學問之功不可誣
然聖賢之道未必有也韓琦垂紳正笏不
動聲色而措天下於太山之安岳飛盡忠
報國屢奏捷功而致中原有幾復之勢雖
其識見之大不可及然道學之傳莫之許
也斯文天啓兩程勃興上接孔孟之傳下
開紫陽之緒道學之正印以承王道之大
體以立使得其時而為之則功業之盛當
===
亞伊呂豈在諸公下哉然二子師授之原
无同造詣之途雖異故其議論之間無復
□之辯朱子稱其人則曰兩夫子述其言
□子以其道之同也至謂明道純粹
蓋其渾然天成之妙明道之於顔
一□相似矣謂伊川英發如孟子則其命
世亞聖之才伊川之於孟子或未及焉其
源同也故稱其同者非誣隨語其所以同
也其成異也故稱其異者非抵惜辯其所
punctuated:
無所悔。嘗彌之屢役屢黜，以身繫天下之安危，去就無所累。雖其學問之功不可誣，然聖賢之道未必有也。韓琦垂紳正笏，不動聲色，而措天下於太山之安；岳飛盡忠報國，屢奏捷功，而致中原有幾復之勢。雖其識見之大不可及，然道學之傳莫之許也。
斯文天啓，兩程勃興，上接孔孟之傳，下開紫陽之緒。道學之正印以承，王道之大體以立。使得其時而為之，則功業之盛當亞伊呂，豈在諸公下哉？然二子師授之原无同，造詣之途雖異，故其議論之間無復□之辯。朱子稱其人則曰兩夫子，述其言□子，以其道之同也。至謂明道純粹，蓋其渾然天成之妙，明道之於顔一□相似矣。謂伊川英發如孟子，則其命世亞聖之才，伊川之於孟子或未及焉。其源同也，故稱其同者非誣，隨語其所以同也；其成異也，故稱其異者非抵，惜辯其所
translation_en:
…without regret. Chang Mizhi [?] repeatedly served and was repeatedly dismissed; the security or peril of the realm depended upon him, yet neither leaving office nor taking it encumbered him. Although his achievements in learning cannot be denied, he did not necessarily possess the Way of the sages and worthies. Han Qi, with his sash hanging down and his audience tablet held upright, brought the realm to a security as firm as Mount Tai without betraying any agitation in voice or expression. Yue Fei served his country with utmost loyalty and repeatedly reported victories, bringing the Central Plain close to recovery. Although the breadth of their discernment was beyond others’ reach, neither was acknowledged as an heir to the Learning of the Way.
Heaven opened the way for this cultural tradition, and the two Cheng brothers rose to prominence. They continued the transmission from Confucius and Mencius above and opened the line leading to Ziyang (Zhu Xi) below. Thus the authentic seal of the Learning of the Way was inherited, and the essential framework of the Kingly Way established. Had they obtained the opportunity to put it into practice, the greatness of their achievements would have ranked next to those of Yi Yin and Lü Shang. How could they have ranked below the gentlemen just mentioned? Yet the origins of the two masters’ instruction were not the same [?], and although their paths of attainment differed, in their discussions there was no further dispute over □ [?]. Master Zhu referred to them as “the two masters”; when recounting their words, [the text is defective: □子], because their Way was the same. As for calling Mingdao (Cheng Hao) pure and unmixed, this referred to the wondrous quality of his integrated, heaven-given nature. Mingdao resembled Yan Hui in [an unclear respect: 一□]. As for calling Yichuan (Cheng Yi) brilliant and vigorous like Mencius, in the talent that made Mencius an epochal figure and the Second Sage, Yichuan perhaps did not measure up to him. Their source was the same; thus those who spoke of their sameness did not misrepresent them, but explained wherein they were alike [?]. Their attainments differed; thus those who spoke of their differences did not disparage them, but distinguished wherein they… [?]

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
以異也以道相正夫豈得而無言哉中州
之士體用之學大率如此然皆非後學之
敢輕言亦非後學之所能學也雖然論學
問則當以明道為標的論功業則當以魏
公為準繩學問不期於明道是棄其身者
也功業不期於魏公是忘其國者也由程
韓之學問功業等而上之尚何伊尹太公
之德業有不可到之哉高山景行之思未
嘗敢忘於須史之頃也
===
第四問
崔銳
同考試官訓導郭　批　悉數古昔善惡之
鑒戒而未復設議以寓將來文章之有益於
人者如此哉
同考試官學正李　批　條荅詳明而筆力
健詞氣壯無忝作家
考試官教授李　批　策有事實可刋
考試官教授濮　批　條荅無遺
punctuated:
以異也。以道相正，夫豈得而無言哉？中州之士，體用之學大率如此。然皆非後學之敢輕言，亦非後學之所能學也。雖然，論學問則當以明道為標的，論功業則當以魏公為準繩。學問不期於明道，是棄其身者也；功業不期於魏公，是忘其國者也。由程韓之學問功業等而上之，尚何伊尹太公之德業有不可到之哉？高山景行之思，未嘗敢忘於須史之頃也。

第四問
崔銳
同考試官訓導郭批：悉數古昔善惡之鑒戒，而未復設議以寓將來，文章之有益於人者如此哉！
同考試官學正李批：條荅詳明，而筆力健，詞氣壯，無忝作家。
考試官教授李批：策有事實，可刋。
考試官教授濮批：條荅無遺。
translation_en:
…wherein they differ. In correcting one another according to the Way, how could they refrain from speaking? Such, in broad outline, was the learning concerning substance and function among the scholars of the Central Plain. Yet none of this is something that a later student would dare discuss lightly, or could readily emulate. Nevertheless, in discussing learning, one should take Mingdao as the target; in discussing achievements in public service, one should take the Duke of Wei as the standard. To pursue learning without aspiring to Mingdao is to abandon oneself; to pursue public achievements without aspiring to the Duke of Wei is to forget one’s country. Advancing step by step from the learning and achievements of Cheng and Han, what could remain unattainable in the virtue and accomplishments of Yi Yin and Taigong? I have never dared, even for an instant [?], to forget my aspiration to look up to the lofty mountain and follow the great road.

Fourth Question
Cui Rui

Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He enumerates fully the examples of good and evil from antiquity that offer instruction and warning, yet does not further develop an argument bearing on the future [?]. Such is the benefit that writing brings to others!”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “His answers to the individual points are detailed and clear; his brushwork is vigorous and his language forceful. He is worthy of being called an accomplished writer.”

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “The policy essay contains factual substance and merits printing.”

Examiner Pu, Professor, comments: “His answers to the individual points omit nothing.”

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
制刑有輕重皆所以為天下之防用刑有
善惡皆可以為天下之鑒蓋教以祗德刑
以弼教制刑雖有重輕無非所以防天下
之人使之去惡而從善率性而循理用夫
刑者使皆體夫刑期無刑式敬由獄之言
而不二三其心高下其手尚何有刑罰不
中而壞天下之防哉請因明聞而膝陳之
刑為生殺人之具死者不可復生斷者不
可復續故大易一則曰雷電噬嗑先王以
===
明罰勑法二則曰雷電豐君子以折獄致
刑刑固為天下所重以唐虞盛世而猶讚
士師文武聖君而尚專庶獄輔治弼教不
可無刑而亦不可不慎也考之古昔司刑
之官善者固有而惡者亦多以其善者言
之爭辨孝婦殺姑之冤而致天雨歲豐之
感此東海于公之仁也拜相封侯子孫貴
盛人以為仁德之報矣郭躬在穎川三十
年存心忠誠斷獄平恕前事等數百於寸
punctuated:
制刑有輕重，皆所以為天下之防；用刑有善惡，皆可以為天下之鑒。蓋教以祗德，刑以弼教。制刑雖有重輕，無非所以防天下之人，使之去惡而從善，率性而循理。用夫刑者，使皆體夫「刑期無刑」、「式敬由獄」之言，而不二三其心，高下其手，尚何有刑罰不中而壞天下之防哉？請因明聞而膝陳之。
刑為生殺人之具，死者不可復生，斷者不可復續。故《大易》一則曰：「雷電，噬嗑；先王以明罰勑法。」二則曰：「雷電，豐；君子以折獄致刑。」刑固為天下所重。以唐虞盛世而猶讚士師，文武聖君而尚專庶獄，輔治弼教，不可無刑，而亦不可不慎也。
考之古昔司刑之官，善者固有，而惡者亦多。以其善者言之，爭辨孝婦殺姑之冤，而致天雨歲豐之感，此東海于公之仁也。拜相封侯，子孫貴盛，人以為仁德之報矣。郭躬在穎川三十年，存心忠誠，斷獄平恕，前事等數百於寸
translation_en:
Punishments are established with differing degrees of severity, all to serve as restraints for the realm; punishments are administered well or badly, and both can serve as lessons for the realm. Teaching inculcates reverence for virtue, and punishment assists teaching. Although established punishments differ in severity, their sole purpose is to restrain the people of the realm, causing them to abandon evil and follow goodness, accord with their nature, and observe principle. If all who administer punishment embodied the sayings, “The aim of punishment is to bring about the absence of punishment” and “Be reverent in handling judicial cases,” neither wavering in their intentions nor manipulating judgments, how could inappropriate punishments undermine the restraints of the realm? Permit me, addressing your enlightened hearing, to set this forth on my knees.
Punishment is an instrument for deciding whether people live or die. The dead cannot be brought back to life, nor can severed limbs be reattached. Thus the great Book of Changes says in one place: “Thunder and lightning: Biting Through. The former kings thereby clarified punishments and put the laws in order.” In another it says: “Thunder and lightning: Abundance. The gentleman thereby adjudicates cases and imposes punishments.” Punishment is indeed a matter of grave concern to the realm. Even in the flourishing age of Tang and Yu, the judicial officer was praised; even the sage kings Wen and Wu devoted particular attention to judicial cases. To support government and assist teaching, punishment is indispensable, yet it must also be used with care.
Examining the officials responsible for punishment in antiquity, we find that there were certainly good ones, but also many bad ones. To speak of the good: arguing against the wrongful accusation that a filial daughter-in-law had killed her mother-in-law, and thereby eliciting Heaven’s response of rain and an abundant harvest—this was the benevolence of Master Yu of Donghai. His descendants became chief ministers and were enfeoffed as marquises, attaining high rank and prosperity; people regarded this as the recompense for his benevolent virtue. Guo Gong spent thirty years in Yingchuan, maintaining a loyal and sincere heart and deciding cases with fairness and forbearance. The preceding affairs numbered several hundred [?] …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
公有不亟哉每赦十二使臣之罪而得刑
部如議之命此判官孫立節之直也還管
進秩嗣續顯榮人以爲立節之報矣盛吉
爲廷尉十二年決獄無滯天下稱平而白
鵲巢樹於立節有不同哉至若出獄數爹
母乃喜笑無所辯世即怒嗔非爲不疑
爲京兆尹而行縣以錄囚乎戒世吾子毋
即感悟爲陳人倫于亦成孝非仇覽爲蒲
亭長而以德化陳元乎又若蘇瓊之爲清
===
河太守因乙晋明兄弟爭田而諭以兄弟
難得田地易求致其叩頭洒淚而復同居
之義李素立之爲御史都護因唐高祖欲
殺小罪而諫以法若動搖民無所措是以
恩感夷人而致餽獻立誠他如綿洒推官
歐陽觀也夜治官書屢發嗟嘆而妻乃疑
問觀語之曰此爲死獄我求其生可生而
聽人至於死此觀之不爲也嗣子賢貴豈
無微哉開封功曹陳洎也章獻臨朝族人
punctuated: 公有不亟哉？每赦十二使臣之罪，而得刑部如議之命，此判官孫立節之直也。還管進秩，嗣續顯榮，人以爲立節之報矣。盛吉爲廷尉十二年，決獄無滯，天下稱平，而白鵲巢樹，於立節有不同哉？至若出獄數爹，母乃喜笑；無所辯世，即怒嗔，非爲不疑爲京兆尹而行縣以錄囚乎？戒世吾子，毋即感悟，爲陳人倫，于亦成孝，非仇覽爲蒲亭長而以德化陳元乎？又若蘇瓊之爲清河太守，因乙晋明兄弟爭田，而諭以兄弟難得、田地易求，致其叩頭洒淚而復同居之義。李素立之爲御史都護，因唐高祖欲殺小罪，而諫以法若動搖、民無所措，是以恩感夷人而致餽獻立誠。他如綿洒推官歐陽觀也，夜治官書，屢發嗟嘆，而妻乃疑問。觀語之曰：「此爲死獄，我求其生。可生而聽人至於死，此觀之不爲也。」嗣子賢貴，豈無微哉？開封功曹陳洎也，章獻臨朝，族人
translation_en:
…could this gentleman have failed to attain distinction [?]? He repeatedly pardoned the offenses of twelve emissaries and obtained an order from the Ministry of Justice approving his recommendation: such was the uprightness of the administrative assistant Sun Lijie. Restored to office [?] and advanced in rank, with his descendants achieving distinction and honor, he was regarded as having received the reward for maintaining his integrity. Sheng Ji served as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement for twelve years, deciding cases without delay. All under Heaven praised his impartiality, and white magpies nested in his trees. Was his case any different from Lijie’s?
When the number released from prison was large [?], his mother would smile with pleasure; when there were no cases vindicated [?], she would become angry. Was this not Buyi, who, as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, toured the counties to review prisoners’ cases? He admonished “my son” [?], whereupon there was an awakening [?]; he explained the human relationships, and filial conduct resulted [?]. Was this not Qiu Lan, who, as head of Pu station, transformed Chen Yuan through virtue?
Likewise, when Su Qiong was governor of Qinghe, Yi Jinming and his brother disputed over farmland. He instructed them that brothers were hard to obtain, whereas land was easy to acquire. This moved them to knock their heads on the ground and shed tears, and to resume living together in righteousness. When Li Suli served as censor and protector-general, Emperor Gaozu of Tang wished to execute someone for a minor offense. Li remonstrated that if the law became unstable, the people would not know how to conduct themselves. Through his kindness he moved the non-Han peoples, prompting them to offer gifts and demonstrate sincerity.
Another example was Ouyang Guan, judge of Mian[?]. At night, while working through official documents, he repeatedly sighed, until his wife, puzzled, questioned him. Guan told her: “This is a capital case. I am seeking a way to preserve his life. To allow someone to go to his death when he could be spared is something I, Guan, will not do.” His son became worthy and eminent: could there have been no hidden cause for this?
There was also Chen Ji, Merit Officer of Kaifeng. When Empress Zhangxian presided over court affairs, a member of her clan…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
殺卒而吏欲掩飾洎捕之曰彼實冤死待
我而伸懼罪而驗冤不以實此洎之不肖
也名聲赫奕豈不虞哉之數公者皆用刑
之善者焉以其無者言之撓法而活其私
所愛曲法而滅其私所憎此周陽由為郡
守之偏酷後竟棄市理之宜也張湯為大
中大夫而舞智弄人從暴治獄巧排陷於
大臣逞威福於私己讓陽由不多哉捕姦
而連逮千餘家錄囚而流血十餘里此王
===
温舒為郡守之殘刻後亦自盡天之厭也
索元禮為武后推使而曲順上旨文戮善
人作鐵籠以訊囚窮根柢於連坐違温舒
不遠哉以至注醯困鼻溺矢囚寢來俊臣
為御史中丞然也厥後抉目摘肝宜西市
人之恨其殘而快其死焉承詔治獄大肆
誅殺周興為秋官侍郎然也厥後黨身殞
命宜天下人之喜其敗而洩其忿也又若
李林甫引吉温於門下吉温乃與羅希奭
punctuated:
殺卒，而吏欲掩飾，洎捕之曰：「彼實冤死，待我而伸。懼罪而驗冤不以實，此洎之不肖也。」名聲赫奕，豈不虞哉？之數公者，皆用刑之善者焉。
以其無者言之，撓法而活其私所愛，曲法而滅其私所憎，此周陽由為郡守之偏酷，後竟棄市，理之宜也。張湯為大中大夫，而舞智弄人，從暴治獄，巧排陷於大臣，逞威福於私己，讓陽由不多哉？捕姦而連逮千餘家，錄囚而流血十餘里，此王温舒為郡守之殘刻，後亦自盡，天之厭也。索元禮為武后推使，而曲順上旨，文戮善人，作鐵籠以訊囚，窮根柢於連坐，違温舒不遠哉？以至注醯困鼻，溺矢囚寢，來俊臣為御史中丞然也。厥後抉目摘肝，宜西市人之恨其殘而快其死焉。承詔治獄，大肆誅殺，周興為秋官侍郎然也。厥後黨身殞命，宜天下人之喜其敗而洩其忿也。又若李林甫引吉温於門下，吉温乃與羅希奭
translation_en:
…killed a soldier, and the clerks sought to conceal the matter. Chen Ji arrested the culprit, saying: “That man truly died unjustly and depends upon me for redress. If, fearing punishment, I investigated this injustice without reporting the truth, that would show my own unworthiness.” His reputation shone brilliantly—was this not to be expected [?]? These gentlemen were all adept at administering punishments.
Turning to those who lacked this virtue: bending the law to spare those he personally loved and twisting it to destroy those he personally hated—such was the partiality and cruelty of Zhouyang You as commandery governor. That he was ultimately executed in the marketplace was what justice required. Zhang Tang, as Grand Palace Grandee, deployed his cunning to manipulate others and conducted judicial proceedings with brutality. He ingeniously contrived to bring down and entrap high ministers, arrogating to himself the power to punish and reward. How little he fell short of Zhouyang You! Arresting wrongdoers and thereby implicating and detaining more than a thousand households, reviewing prisoners’ cases until blood flowed for more than ten li—such was the cruelty of Wang Wenshu as commandery governor. That he too ultimately took his own life showed Heaven’s abhorrence of him. Suo Yuanli, as an investigating commissioner under Empress Wu, unscrupulously complied with the sovereign’s wishes and contrived legal grounds for executing good people. He made an iron cage for interrogating prisoners and pursued chains of collective implication to their very roots. How little he differed from Wang Wenshu! Going so far as to pour vinegar into the nose to impede breathing and to befoul prisoners’ sleeping quarters with urine and excrement [?]—such were Lai Junchen’s acts as Vice Censor-in-Chief. Later, his eyes were gouged out and his liver torn out. No wonder the people in the western marketplace, hating his cruelty, rejoiced at his death. Receiving imperial commands to adjudicate cases and indulging in wholesale executions—such were Zhou Xing’s acts as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Autumn [Justice]. Later, he lost his life through factional involvement [?]. No wonder people throughout the realm rejoiced at his downfall and vented their anger. Then there was Li Linfu, who brought Ji Wen into his circle; Ji Wen thereupon joined with Luo Xishi…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
推鞫詔獄以虐相尚時稱鉏網之名此吉
温之酷暴無似也王安石遷蔡確爲御史
而確遂希王安石鞫問城卒鍛鍊而成日
肆羅織之毒此蔡確之殘虐無倫也安惇
爲御史而密設傾揺之奸計雜治同文之
謗獄致忠良殆盡後來劉時而二子貶死
史臣列與蔡京同傳非直筆乎万俟卨爲
提點而首劾忠良之逗留竟致父子之寃
死使和議遂成後不旋踵而忤心奸檜謫
===
死歸州史臣編與秦檜同傳非公論乎之
數人者皆用刑之惡者焉是則一善一惡
昭著如此而皆所以爲天下後世之鑒戒
也雖然又有說焉今之議者以爲祥則忠
厚而近於善嚴猛則勵力而近於惡非也
慈祥本善而流於姑息則不善嚴猛非惡
以過於慘酷則爲惡不有折中之道乎亦
惟不狃於私不撓於勢輕不至縱重不至
苛苟不當刑不殺怒於然寃在所必刑不
punctuated:
推鞫詔獄，以虐相尚，時稱鉏網之名，此吉温之酷暴無似也。王安石遷蔡確爲御史，而確遂希王安石，鞫問城卒，鍛鍊而成，日肆羅織之毒，此蔡確之殘虐無倫也。安惇爲御史，而密設傾揺之奸計，雜治同文之謗獄，致忠良殆盡。後來劉時而二子貶死，史臣列與蔡京同傳，非直筆乎？万俟卨爲提點，而首劾忠良之逗留，竟致父子之寃死，使和議遂成。後不旋踵而忤心奸檜，謫死歸州，史臣編與秦檜同傳，非公論乎？之數人者，皆用刑之惡者焉。是則一善一惡，昭著如此，而皆所以爲天下後世之鑒戒也。
雖然，又有說焉。今之議者以爲祥則忠厚而近於善，嚴猛則勵力而近於惡，非也。慈祥本善，而流於姑息則不善；嚴猛非惡，以過於慘酷則爲惡。不有折中之道乎？亦惟不狃於私，不撓於勢，輕不至縱，重不至苛。苟不當刑，不殺怒於然寃；在所必刑，不
translation_en:
…interrogated prisoners in cases ordered by imperial edict, each striving to surpass the other in cruelty. At the time this was called the “hoeing net” [?]. Such was Ji Wen’s unparalleled brutality. Wang Anshi promoted Cai Que to Censor, and Cai Que then sought to please Wang Anshi by interrogating soldiers of the city garrison and fabricating a case against them, daily unleashing the poison of concocted charges. Such was Cai Que’s matchless cruelty. Serving as Censor, An Dun secretly devised treacherous schemes to bring others down and participated in investigating the Tongwen slander case, bringing almost all the loyal and worthy men involved to ruin. Later, “Liu Shi and the two sons died in banishment” [?]. The official historians placed him in the same biography as Cai Jing: was this not forthright historical writing? Moqi Xie, serving as Judicial Commissioner, took the lead in impeaching a loyal and worthy man for delaying his advance. Ultimately he caused the unjust deaths of father and son, enabling the peace agreement to be concluded. Soon afterward he offended the treacherous Qin Hui and died in exile in Guizhou. The official historians placed him in the same biography as Qin Hui: was this not an impartial judgment? These several men were all evil in their administration of punishment. Thus good and evil stand out so clearly, both providing lessons and warnings for the world and later generations.
Nevertheless, there is more to say. Those who discuss the matter today consider kindness loyal and generous, and therefore close to goodness, while severity is forceful and strenuous, and therefore close to evil. This is wrong. Kindness is fundamentally good, but when it degenerates into indulgence, it is no longer good. Severity is not evil, but when it goes too far and becomes cruelty, it becomes evil. Is there not a balanced course? It consists simply in neither yielding to private interests nor bending before power, ensuring that leniency does not become laxity and that severity does not become harshness. If someone does not deserve punishment, one must not kill out of anger and thereby cause injustice [?]; where punishment is necessary, one must not …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
樹私於恩地一遵帝王之訓以無忝天地
之心耳愚不敏倘責司刑不敢不以此言
□勵
第五問
李東熙
同考試官訓導鄭　批〔有考據有識見非博雅之士不及此〕
同考試官學正李　批〔議論弘暢斟酌詳審與牽制拘牽肆為妄說者不侔〕
考試官教授李　批〔條答治河事宜切指諸學臨筆之弊〕
===
考試官教授　　批〔治水一策鑿鑿有餘言不徒資考而□此可與習者道〕
審天下之勢者不鑿以人為成天下之功
者不專於已出何也勢因乎天而在□者
□可以不順功成於人而在人者不□□
不公故君子之處事不患乎無其智所□
者不能循其勢而失之鑿不憂乎無其功
punctuated:
樹私於恩地，一遵帝王之訓，以無忝天地之心耳。愚不敏，倘責司刑，不敢不以此言□勵。

第五問
李東熙
同考試官訓導鄭　批〔有考據，有識見，非博雅之士不及此。〕
同考試官學正李　批〔議論弘暢，斟酌詳審，與牽制拘牽、肆為妄說者不侔。〕
考試官教授李　批〔條答治河事宜，切指諸學臨筆之弊。〕
考試官教授　　批〔治水一策，鑿鑿有餘言，不徒資考，而□此可與習者道。〕

審天下之勢者，不鑿以人為；成天下之功者，不專於已出。何也？勢因乎天，而在□者，□可以不順；功成於人，而在人者，不□□不公。故君子之處事，不患乎無其智，所□者不能循其勢而失之鑿；不憂乎無其功
translation_en:
…nor allow personal favoritism in bestowing grace [?], but follow wholly the teachings of the emperors and kings, so as not to fall short of the intentions of Heaven and Earth. Though I am dull-witted, should I be charged with administering punishments, I would not dare fail to use these words to spur myself on [?].

Fifth Policy Question
Li Dongxi

Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “There is supporting evidence and discernment here; only a broadly learned and cultivated scholar could attain this.”
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The argument is expansive and fluent, the deliberation thorough and careful. It is unlike the work of those who are constrained and hidebound, or who recklessly advance unfounded opinions.”
Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “He answers point by point on measures for managing the river, and incisively identifies the shortcomings of the various students when they take up their brushes.”
Examiner, Professor [name not supplied], comments: “This policy essay on water management is cogent and has much more to say. It does not merely provide material for consideration; [illegible] this can be discussed with those versed in the subject [?].”

Those who assess the configuration of affairs in the realm do not distort it through human contrivance; those who accomplish great works in the realm do not insist that everything originate with themselves. Why is this? The configuration of affairs derives from Heaven, and what lies in [illegible] cannot but be followed [?]; achievements are accomplished through people, and what rests with people must be handled impartially [?]. Thus, when the gentleman conducts affairs, he does not worry that he lacks wisdom; what he [illegible] is that, by failing to follow the configuration of affairs, he may err through forced contrivance. He does not worry that he lacks accomplishments…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
所憂者未能參諸人而失之專孟子曰所
惡於智者爲其鑿也中庸曰爲政在人參
二曰爲政不在於用一己之長論治河者
亦審諸此而已舍此而他求未見其有濟
也請爲執事言之夫水在天地間貫道化
之始鉅而四海次而四瀆治之而順其理
皆有以益於國而澤乎民是莫不有利也
治之而失其道適足以病夫國而傷夫民
是莫不有害也然求之書質之史而驗之
===
於事則水之爲利固莫如河水之爲害又
孰大於河哉嘗考河之爲水濫觴崑崙洶
湧萬里莫知紀極大禹疏導之時河自永
經於汴而洛汭實河之故道也觀禹貢導
河東過洛汭至於大伾北過洚水至於大
陸又北播爲九河同爲逆河入於海之文
可知矣降至戰國各以隄防自固河水東
抵齊隄則反而西泛趙魏自河內黎陽至
魏郡昭陽以東百餘里間河水再西三東
punctuated:
所憂者未能參諸人而失之專。孟子曰：「所惡於智者，爲其鑿也。」中庸曰：「爲政在人。」參二曰，爲政不在於用一己之長。論治河者亦審諸此而已，舍此而他求，未見其有濟也。請爲執事言之。
夫水在天地間，貫道化之始，鉅而四海，次而四瀆，治之而順其理，皆有以益於國而澤乎民，是莫不有利也。治之而失其道，適足以病夫國而傷夫民，是莫不有害也。然求之書，質之史，而驗之於事，則水之爲利固莫如河，水之爲害又孰大於河哉？嘗考河之爲水，濫觴崑崙，洶湧萬里，莫知紀極。大禹疏導之時，河自永經於汴，而洛汭實河之故道也。觀禹貢「導河，東過洛汭，至於大伾，北過洚水，至於大陸，又北播爲九河，同爲逆河，入於海」之文，可知矣。降至戰國，各以隄防自固，河水東抵齊隄，則反而西泛趙魏。自河內黎陽至魏郡昭陽，以東百餘里間，河水再西三東。
translation_en:
…What he worries about is failing to consult others and thereby falling into arbitrary action. Mencius said: “What is objectionable about cleverness is its forced contrivance.” The Doctrine of the Mean says: “The conduct of government depends on people.” Taking these two sayings together [?], governing does not consist in employing one’s own strengths alone. Those who discuss controlling the Yellow River need only examine these principles. I have yet to see any benefit in abandoning them and seeking elsewhere. Allow me to explain this to you, sir.
Water exists between Heaven and Earth, running through the beginnings of the transformations of the Way [?]. The largest bodies are the Four Seas, followed by the Four Watercourses. If they are managed in accordance with their inherent patterns, all can benefit the state and bring blessings to the people: none is without benefit. If their management departs from the proper course, it serves only to afflict the state and harm the people: none is without harm. Yet if we seek evidence in the Book of Documents, check it against the histories, and test it against actual events, surely no watercourse equals the Yellow River in the benefits it brings; and what watercourse exceeds it in the harm it causes? I have examined the Yellow River’s course: it begins as a trickle in Kunlun and surges for ten thousand li, its bounds and limits beyond knowing. When Yu the Great dredged and guided it, the river ran from Yong [?] through Bian, and Luorui was indeed on its former course. This can be seen from the passage in the Tribute of Yu: “He guided the Yellow River east past Luorui to Dapi, north past the Jiang River to Dalu, then farther north, where it divided into the Nine Rivers; these united as the Ni River and entered the sea.” By the Warring States period, each state protected itself with embankments. When the Yellow River reached Qi’s embankments to the east, it turned back and flooded Zhao and Wei to the west. In the stretch extending more than a hundred li eastward from Liyang in Henei to Zhaoyang in Wei Commandery, the Yellow River turned west twice and east three times…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
不勝迫阨故周定王五年河徙砱礫則漸
遷於東南而不循故道及秦始皇使王賁
攻魏決河溝之水灌大梁之城其所決遂
大而不可復補漢元光間故道嘗復而不
能久至於有宋始復南決而莫能救南渡
之後遂由彭城合汴泗以入淮而向之故
道又失矣逮至於今則由汴城而亳而自
渦口達淮而向之故道愈失矣禹貢之河
道豈今日之河道乎蓋
===
國朝正統以前河決北而勢趨於南故決於
滎陽東越汴城南而遶還入淮是時汴城
在河之北弘治以來又決於南而勢趨於北
故決於原武東北過沁水溢流爲一延及
張秋之運河自是汴城在河之南矣昔之
害莫切於兗今則切於豫昔之害首受於
衛今則受於汴今歲霖潦連綿河肆決溢
護城之隄雖足捍禦而附郭之家類爲沮
洳當職者之憂孰大於此乎且激悍爲潮
punctuated: 不勝迫阨，故周定王五年，河徙砱礫，則漸遷於東南而不循故道。及秦始皇使王賁攻魏，決河溝之水灌大梁之城，其所決遂大而不可復補。漢元光間，故道嘗復而不能久。至於有宋，始復南決而莫能救。南渡之後，遂由彭城合汴泗以入淮，而向之故道又失矣。逮至於今，則由汴城而亳，而自渦口達淮，而向之故道愈失矣。《禹貢》之河道，豈今日之河道乎？蓋國朝正統以前，河決北而勢趨於南，故決於滎陽，東越汴城南，而遶還入淮。是時汴城在河之北。弘治以來，又決於南而勢趨於北，故決於原武，東北過沁水，溢流爲一，延及張秋之運河。自是汴城在河之南矣。昔之害莫切於兗，今則切於豫；昔之害首受於衛，今則受於汴。今歲霖潦連綿，河肆決溢，護城之隄雖足捍禦，而附郭之家類爲沮洳。當職者之憂，孰大於此乎？且激悍爲潮
translation_en:
…unable to withstand the constriction. Thus, in the fifth year of King Ding of Zhou, the Yellow River shifted to Lingli, gradually moving southeast and ceasing to follow its former course. When the First Emperor of Qin sent Wang Ben to attack Wei, he released the waters of the river and canals to inundate the city of Daliang. The breach then grew so large that it could no longer be repaired. During the Yuanguang era of the Han, the former course was briefly restored, but this did not last. Under the Song, the river again began to breach southward, and no one could remedy it. After the court moved south, the river passed through Pengcheng, joined the Bian and Si rivers, and entered the Huai; its former course was once again lost. By the present day, it passes from Biancheng through Bo and reaches the Huai through Guokou, departing still further from its former course. Can the river course described in the Tribute of Yu possibly be the river course of today?
Before the Zhengtong era of our dynasty, the river breached in the north, but its waters tended southward. Thus it broke through at Xingyang, flowed east past the south of Biancheng, and wound around to enter the Huai. At that time, Biancheng lay north of the river. Since the beginning of the Hongzhi era, it has again breached in the south, but its waters have tended northward. Thus it broke through at Yuanwu, passed northeast across the Qin River, and merged with it in a single flood, extending as far as the transport canal at Zhangqiu. Since then, Biancheng has lain south of the river. Formerly, nowhere suffered more acutely than Yan; now it is Yu that suffers acutely. Formerly, Wei bore the first impact of the damage; now Bian bears it. This year, prolonged rains and flooding have continued without respite, and the river has breached and overflowed unchecked. Although the embankments protecting the city have been sufficient to hold it back, the homes adjoining the city walls have mostly become waterlogged marshland. What greater concern could there be for the officials responsible? Moreover, violent surging is the tide’s [?] …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
之性卑跡為豫之地以彼乘此□□□
無足怪者而惟治之有法耳夫□□□□
□法以禦河道之更變固無不可然河害
於漢而漢不知因其勢害及宋元而宋元
罕能成其功豈不由害之以入為而不因
乎天事之於己出而不公諸人□□淮
國朝建都燕薊漕粟以實京師而必取□江
淮諸郡造閘以制運河而惟□夫□□□
川一決於張秋之口則害及博濟之境□
===
道為之枯涸綱運為之遏絕如國計何鄉
民愚何是誠不可聽之東行而滋□□塞
也茲欲處治得宜不失成法是固愚□之
所欲言亦皆
國家之所已試嘗觀近歲張秋之決工歷
宸慮特遣在廷重臣以主之又分委藩臬諸臣
以輔之而責任得人處治有道先□□□
之地濬祥符之壅以殺其勢繼塞孫家渡
荊隆等六口以截其流而治之者因其勢
punctuated:
之性，卑跡為豫之地，以彼乘此，□□□，無足怪者，而惟治之有法耳。夫□□□□□法，以禦河道之更變，固無不可。然河害於漢，而漢不知因其勢；害及宋元，而宋元罕能成其功。豈不由害之以入為，而不因乎天；事之於己出，而不公諸人？□□淮。
國朝建都燕薊，漕粟以實京師，而必取□江淮諸郡；造閘以制運河，而惟□夫□□□川。一決於張秋之口，則害及博濟之境，□道為之枯涸，綱運為之遏絕，如國計何？鄉民愚何？是誠不可聽之東行而滋□□塞也。茲欲處治得宜，不失成法，是固愚□之所欲言，亦皆國家之所已試。嘗觀近歲張秋之決，工歷宸慮，特遣在廷重臣以主之，又分委藩臬諸臣以輔之，而責任得人，處治有道。先□□□之地，濬祥符之壅，以殺其勢；繼塞孫家渡、荊隆等六口，以截其流，而治之者因其勢，
translation_en:
…is its nature, while the terrain of Henan is low-lying [?]. When the former bears down upon the latter, [three illegible characters], there is nothing surprising about this; what matters is having proper methods of controlling it. Now, [five illegible characters] methods for coping with changes in the river’s course are certainly admissible. Yet the river caused harm under the Han, and the Han did not know how to work with its momentum. Its harm continued into the Song and Yuan, but those dynasties seldom succeeded in controlling it. Was this not because they impaired it through human intervention [?], rather than following Heaven, and made these undertakings proceed from themselves rather than opening them to others? [Two illegible characters] Huai [?].
Our dynasty established its capital in the Yan–Ji region. It transports grain by water to provision the capital, necessarily drawing [illegible character] upon the prefectures of the Yangzi and Huai regions. It built sluices to regulate the Grand Canal, but [passage partly illegible and doubtful] river. Once a breach occurs at Zhangqiu, the damage extends to the Bo–Ji region. The [illegible character] channel dries up, and grain transport convoys are halted. What then becomes of the state’s finances? And what of the local people [?]? We certainly cannot let it flow eastward and aggravate [two illegible characters] obstruction [?]. Now, to manage it appropriately without abandoning established methods is indeed what I, in my ignorance [illegible character], wish to discuss; these are also all measures that the state has already tried. Consider the breach at Zhangqiu in recent years: the works engaged the Emperor’s concern [?]. He specially dispatched senior court ministers to take charge, and separately assigned officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions to assist them. Responsibility thus rested with suitable men, and the undertaking was properly managed. First, [three illegible characters] terrain, and they dredged the obstruction at Xiangfu to diminish the force of the water. Next, they blocked the six breaches at Sunjiadu, Jinglong, and other places to cut off its flow. Thus those who controlled it worked with its momentum…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣是故水患既去運渠復通其於前規
法今日之宜亦已審矣然踵大禹之迹以
立治河之方亦各不同彼如釃河之流因
而導之曰疏去河之淤因而濬之曰濬抑
河之暴因而扼之曰塞此前代治河之三
法皆可舉行生地有直紆鑿之以就故道
故道有卑高治之而使相就河身有之難
受水者闢之廣難為岸者禦之減水河有
狂而放曠者制之怒而隳突者殺之此前
===
代疏濬之四端咸可師法漢待詔賈讓治
河三策其上欲決之使通其中欲分水溉
田最下乃為隄防之作雖未嘗行於漢然
參酌而用亦可行於今日宋待制張商英
治水五事一曰行古沙河口二曰復平恩
四埽三曰引河從漳入海四曰開御河東
堤之積五曰開水門泄從駁河東流雖未
得施於宋然採擇而行亦可用於今時尚
文為元廉訪使而獻大策欲於蒲口決處
punctuated:
矣。是故水患既去，運渠復通，其於前規法、今日之宜，亦已審矣。然踵大禹之迹，以立治河之方，亦各不同。彼如釃河之流，因而導之曰疏；去河之淤，因而濬之曰濬；抑河之暴，因而扼之曰塞。此前代治河之三法，皆可舉行。生地有直紆，鑿之以就故道；故道有卑高，治之而使相就；河身有之難受水者，闢之，廣難為岸者，禦之；減水河有狂而放曠者，制之，怒而隳突者，殺之。此前代疏濬之四端，咸可師法。
漢待詔賈讓治河三策，其上欲決之使通，其中欲分水溉田，最下乃為隄防之作。雖未嘗行於漢，然參酌而用，亦可行於今日。宋待制張商英治水五事：一曰行古沙河口，二曰復平恩四埽，三曰引河從漳入海，四曰開御河東堤之積，五曰開水門泄從駁河東流。雖未得施於宋，然採擇而行，亦可用於今時。尚文為元廉訪使，而獻大策，欲於蒲口決處
translation_en:
…Thus the flooding was ended and the transport canal reopened. Due consideration had been given both to earlier precedents and methods and to what was appropriate under present circumstances. Yet methods devised for controlling the Yellow River in the footsteps of Yu the Great have also varied. Dividing the river’s flow and guiding it onward is called channeling; removing its silt and deepening its bed is called dredging; restraining its violence and checking its flow is called blocking. These three methods of river control from earlier dynasties can all be put into practice. Where previously unexcavated ground runs straight or winds about, cut through it to connect with the old course. Where the old course is low or high, work on it to bring its levels into alignment. Where the riverbed has difficulty accommodating the water, widen it; where its breadth makes it difficult to form banks, restrain it [?]. Where flood-diversion channels run wildly and spread unchecked, bring them under control; where they surge furiously and break through, diminish their force. These four aspects of channeling and dredging practiced by earlier dynasties can all serve as models.
Jia Rang, an Expectant Official of the Han dynasty, proposed three plans for controlling the river. His highest-ranked plan was to breach the banks and let the river flow freely; his middle plan was to divert water to irrigate fields; his lowest-ranked plan was the construction of dikes. Although these were never implemented under the Han, they could also be put into practice today if weighed and adapted appropriately. Zhang Shangying, an Edict Attendant of the Song dynasty, proposed five measures for controlling the waters: first, to route the flow through the old Shahe mouth; second, to restore the four fascine embankments at Ping’en; third, to lead the river through the Zhang River into the sea; fourth, to clear the accumulated deposits at the eastern dike of the Yuhe; and fifth, to open sluice gates and discharge the water eastward through the Bohe [?]. Although these measures were not implemented under the Song, selected measures could also be applied today. Shang Wen, serving as a Surveillance Commissioner under the Yuan, submitted a major plan, proposing that at the breach at Pukou…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
築長隄以禦泛溢開淤塞以通漕臨而又
遷民村落以避衝負給民賞以備所費
亦救弊良法也豈徒施於元而已哉賈魯
為元都水使者而陳二策欲於濟陰決處
一則脩築北隄以制水之橫潰一則疏塞
並舉挽河東行以復故道亦嘗試吾謀也
豈徒美於前而止哉
國朝翰林承旨宋濂之論治河而欲分其流
者蓋祖大禹釃為九渠之說而中余闕多
===
為之委之意國子祭酒丘濬之論治河亦
欲不惜棄地不惜動民以成遠大之利擇
任心膂委從便宜以盡疏濬之術是皆折
衷之當而無闕略之患然原其本意求夫
實功孰非因其水勢而不與水爭地以濟
其潰決又孰非委任人才而不勞民從欲
以驗其績用哉為今之計莫若俟水涸之
候纘前日之功河雖不害於漕而必求其
有利於民隄雖已成於北而不使其為塹
punctuated:
築長隄以禦泛溢，開淤塞以通漕臨，而又遷民村落以避衝負，給民賞以備所費，亦救弊良法也，豈徒施於元而已哉？賈魯為元都水使者，而陳二策，欲於濟陰決處，一則脩築北隄以制水之橫潰，一則疏塞並舉，挽河東行以復故道，亦嘗試吾謀也，豈徒美於前而止哉？
國朝翰林承旨宋濂之論治河而欲分其流者，蓋祖大禹釃為九渠之說，而中余闕多為之委之意。國子祭酒丘濬之論治河，亦欲不惜棄地，不惜動民，以成遠大之利；擇任心膂，委從便宜，以盡疏濬之術。是皆折衷之當，而無闕略之患。然原其本意，求夫實功，孰非因其水勢而不與水爭地，以濟其潰決？又孰非委任人才而不勞民從欲，以驗其績用哉？為今之計，莫若俟水涸之候，纘前日之功。河雖不害於漕，而必求其有利於民；隄雖已成於北，而不使其為塹
translation_en:
…to build a long embankment to restrain flooding and clear obstructions caused by silt so as to facilitate grain transport [?]; furthermore, to relocate villages to avoid the force of the current [?], and to grant the people allowances to cover their expenses. These, too, are sound methods of remedying the trouble. Could they be applicable only under the Yuan? When Jia Lu served as Commissioner of Waterways under the Yuan, he presented two proposals concerning the breach at Jiyin: one was to repair and build up the northern embankment to restrain the water from breaking out laterally; the other was to undertake dredging and blocking together, drawing the river eastward to restore its former course. These, too, were once trials of our plans [?]. Could their merit be confined to the past?
When Song Lian, our dynasty’s Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, discussed controlling the river and advocated dividing its flow, he was following the account of Yu the Great dividing the waters into nine channels, while also agreeing with Yu Que’s intention of providing numerous outlets. In his discussion of river control, Qiu Jun, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, likewise advocated being willing to give up land and move people in order to secure substantial, lasting benefits. He urged selecting and appointing trusted men and authorizing them to act as circumstances required, so that the methods of dredging could be fully employed. These were all judicious accommodations, free from the danger of omissions. Yet if we trace their fundamental intentions and seek their practical achievements, which did not follow the tendency of the waters, avoiding competition with water for land, in order to remedy breaches? And which did not entrust capable men with responsibility, avoiding exhausting the people to satisfy personal desires, in order to demonstrate effective results? For present purposes, nothing would be better than to await the season when the waters recede and carry forward the work already accomplished. Although the river does not impede grain transport, we must ensure that it benefits the people; although the embankment has already been completed on the northern side, we must not allow it to become a moat …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
於南滎澤七十里之新河時加疏濬使無
至於淤澱祥符二十里之故道時加開拓
使不至於狹小水既南下勢必橫溢南岸
捍禦尤不可後乘時之隙役民之力相度
沿河地勢建築縷水隄防務使霖潦之雨
有所備泛濫之水無所肆城郭兆萬姓之
憂漕挽資百世之利暫勞而獲永逸小費
而成大功豈不偉哉賈魯舊河已置北隄
之內絕流日久不復論焉此蓋治河之一
===
端耳若夫論道經邦輔理承化之謨欲言
而未有其階也惟執事恕其狂瞽而進之
punctuated: 於南。滎澤七十里之新河，時加疏濬，使無至於淤澱；祥符二十里之故道，時加開拓，使不至於狹小。水既南下，勢必橫溢，南岸捍禦尤不可後。乘時之隙，役民之力，相度沿河地勢，建築縷水隄防，務使霖潦之雨有所備，泛濫之水無所肆。城郭兆萬姓之憂，漕挽資百世之利，暫勞而獲永逸，小費而成大功，豈不偉哉！賈魯舊河已置北隄之內，絕流日久，不復論焉。此蓋治河之一端耳。若夫論道經邦、輔理承化之謨，欲言而未有其階也。惟執事恕其狂瞽而進之。
translation_en: …to the south. The seventy-li stretch of new channel at Xingze should be dredged regularly so that it does not silt up; the twenty-li stretch of old channel at Xiangfu should be widened regularly so that it does not become too narrow. Once the water flows south, its force will inevitably cause it to overflow laterally, so protective works on the southern bank must especially not be delayed. Taking advantage of intervals when conditions permit, employ the people's labor, survey the terrain along the river, and construct embankments closely following the watercourse. Make every effort to provide against prolonged heavy rains and leave floodwaters no opportunity to run unchecked. The city walls portend anxiety for the myriad people [?], while grain transport by water provides benefits for a hundred generations. To obtain lasting ease through temporary toil, and accomplish a great work at small expense—is this not splendid! Jia Lu's old river channel now lies within the northern embankment; its flow has long been cut off, and I shall discuss it no further. This is but one aspect of managing the river. As for plans to deliberate upon the Way and order the realm, assist in governance and carry forward the sovereign's transforming influence, I wish to speak but have not yet had the opportunity. I ask only that you, honored examiners, forgive my rashness and blindness and recommend me for advancement.

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
河南居天地之中士生其間
者洪河高嵩之靈以鍾其秀
明道伊川之傳以宗其學宰
而遺際
明時刑范陶鑄以成其器所以
出而躋台鼎弼
===
聖化者視昔爲有加猗歟盛哉迺
弘治十一年戊午秋八月當
鄉試之期維時藩臬重臣凡
興舉綜理之謀務極精詳而
巡按監察御史李瀚實總其
事先期進諸執事而告之曰
朝廷設科取士品式未周悉以
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

河南居天地之中，士生其間者，洪河高嵩之靈以鍾其秀，明道伊川之傳以宗其學。宰而遺際明時，刑范陶鑄以成其器，所以出而躋台鼎、弼聖化者，視昔爲有加。猗歟，盛哉！迺弘治十一年戊午秋八月，當鄉試之期，維時藩臬重臣，凡興舉綜理之謀，務極精詳，而巡按監察御史李瀚實總其事。先期進諸執事而告之曰：「朝廷設科取士，品式未周，悉以
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

Henan lies at the center of Heaven and Earth. Among the scholars born there, the spiritual potency of the mighty Yellow River and lofty Mount Song concentrates to produce outstanding talent, while the teachings transmitted by Mingdao and Yichuan provide the foundation of their learning. Encountering an enlightened age [?], they are shaped and molded by exemplary standards until their capacities are fully developed. Thus, those who enter service, rise to the highest ministerial offices, and assist the sage emperor’s transforming influence are more numerous than in former times. Ah, how flourishing!

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the eleventh year of Hongzhi, the wuwu year [1498], the time came for the Provincial Examination. The senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions sought the utmost precision and thoroughness in every plan for organizing and managing it, while Li Han, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, held overall responsibility. Before the appointed date, he summoned the officials concerned and told them: “The court establishes examinations to recruit scholars. The rules and standards are not yet comprehensive; in all cases, by means of … [?]

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
裁抑僥倖禮文未隆無以招
徠豪傑乃斟酌事宜拓新貢
院變湫隘為高廣易萑葦以
榱桷厚幣聘之禮豐燕享之
儀士之與是選者真若躍龍
門步瀛洲矣撤棘之晨觀者
數萬計莫不嘖嘖歎文明之
===
盛而得人之多也雖然今日
之所試者文也所未試者行
也文有典雅浮躁行符之昔
唐韓愈以六經之文為諸儒
倡反頹以樸剗偽以真辯𤄊
一出於正其徒李翺輩從而
效之文體至元和而益工宋
punctuated:
裁抑僥倖，禮文未隆，無以招徠豪傑。」乃斟酌事宜，拓新貢院，變湫隘為高廣，易萑葦以榱桷，厚幣聘之禮，豐燕享之儀。士之與是選者，真若躍龍門、步瀛洲矣。撤棘之晨，觀者數萬計，莫不嘖嘖歎文明之盛而得人之多也。
雖然，今日之所試者文也，所未試者行也。文有典雅、浮躁，行符之。昔唐韓愈以六經之文為諸儒倡，反頹以樸，剗偽以真，辯𤄊一出於正。其徒李翺輩從而效之，文體至元和而益工。宋
translation_en:
…to curb those seeking success through mere good fortune. If ceremonial observances are insufficiently elaborate, there is no means of attracting outstanding men.” Accordingly, he considered what circumstances required and expanded and renovated the examination compound, transforming its low, cramped quarters into lofty, spacious buildings and replacing reeds with rafters and beams. He increased the gifts presented when inviting examiners and made the ceremonial banquets more lavish. The scholars selected on this occasion truly seemed to have leapt the Dragon Gate and set foot on Yingzhou, the isle of immortals. On the morning when the thorn barriers were removed, spectators numbered in the tens of thousands. All exclaimed in admiration at the flourishing of literary culture and the abundance of talent obtained.
Nevertheless, what has been tested today is literary composition; what has not been tested is conduct. Writing may be classical and elegant or frivolous and impetuous, and conduct corresponds to it. Formerly, Han Yu of the Tang took the writings of the Six Classics as his model in leading the scholars. He countered decadence with simplicity and rooted out falsity with truth; his arguments [?] proceeded entirely from what was correct. His followers, including Li Ao, followed and emulated him, and literary style became increasingly accomplished during the Yuanhe era. In the Song dynasty, …

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
劉幾爲文險怪歐陽脩知貢
舉決意痛懲凡爲新文者一
切棄黜時體爲之一變文章
至嘉祐而始盛然則轉移之
機在作興操柄者之何如耳
故二子力主之讅示較文之
後朝夕披閱以思辭之華實
===
理之醇漓別白之咀嚼之皆
有典雅而無浮躁
聖化涵養之深且久有足徵矣嗚
呼法式之嚴密去取之公明
凡我在位當事者若無憾焉
不知諸士榮膺斯舉何如其
爲報稱耶茹商山之薇籲知
punctuated:
劉幾爲文險怪，歐陽脩知貢舉，決意痛懲，凡爲新文者，一切棄黜，時體爲之一變，文章至嘉祐而始盛。然則轉移之機，在作興操柄者之何如耳。故二子力主之。讅示較文之後，朝夕披閱，以思辭之華實、理之醇漓，別白之，咀嚼之，皆有典雅而無浮躁。聖化涵養之深且久，有足徵矣。
嗚呼！法式之嚴密，去取之公明，凡我在位當事者，若無憾焉。不知諸士榮膺斯舉，何如其爲報稱耶？茹商山之薇，籲知
translation_en:
…Liu Ji wrote in a bizarre and outlandish style. When Ouyang Xiu directed the examinations, he resolved to curb this severely: all who wrote in the new style were rejected. The prevailing literary style consequently changed, and literary composition began to flourish in the Jiayou era. Thus, the means of bringing about such a transformation depend upon those who encourage learning and hold authority. The two gentlemen therefore firmly championed this. After the scrutiny and assessment of the compositions [?], they read them morning and evening, considering the ornament and substance of their language and the purity or dilution of their principles, distinguishing these carefully and pondering them thoroughly. All displayed classical elegance, without frivolity or impetuosity. This sufficiently attests to the profound and enduring nurture afforded by the sage emperor’s transforming influence.
Ah! In the rigor and precision of the rules, and the impartiality and discernment of acceptance and rejection, all of us holding office and responsible for this undertaking may feel that we have no cause for regret. Yet I wonder how you gentlemen, honored with selection in this examination, will repay that distinction fittingly. Eating the wild vetch of Mount Shang, calling out in recognition [?]…

title: 弘治十一年河南鄉試錄
text:
德周矧士
聖世而沐
清化誦詩讀書
知所以報稱
儋爵享受
恩遇祿食之隆必
實文而華
===
國以實行而濟
而庶幾可言
書以俟之
應天府儒學
punctuated:
德周，矧士聖世而沐清化，誦詩讀書，知所以報稱。儋爵享受恩遇祿食之隆，必實文而華國，以實行而濟，而庶幾可言。書以俟之。

應天府儒學
translation_en:
…the virtue of Zhou [?]. How much more should scholars living in a sagely age and benefiting from its pure transforming influence, reciting the Odes and reading the Documents, know how to repay these blessings fittingly. Bearing rank [?] and enjoying generous imperial favor and official emoluments, they must give substance to their writing and thereby bring glory to the state, supplementing it with actual conduct. Only then, perhaps, can they speak of having made a fitting return. I write this in anticipation of their doing so.

The Confucian School of Yingtian Prefecture.
